descriptions.text:
Job Announcement
Finance Intern

Company: DriverAI
Location: Remote / Hybrid, based on business need
Employment Type: Internship - Part-Time or Full-Time
Application: Send resume and optional portfolio/work samples to Apply@DriverAI.io

About DriverAI
DriverAI is developing intelligent indoor navigation, AI-enabled analytics, and data-driven product experiences for complex indoor environments. Our team combines software, artificial intelligence, computer vision, cloud services, business analytics, and operational strategy to support commercial and future government opportunities.
About the Role
We are seeking a Finance Intern to support budgeting, expense tracking, financial analysis, reporting, vendor documentation, and business operations. This internship is ideal for a detail-oriented student or early-career professional who wants practical finance experience in a technology startup environment.
What You Will Do
Assist with budget tracking, expense summaries, cash flow support, and variance analysis.
Help organize invoices, subscriptions, vendor information, software costs, procurement records, and project-related financial documentation.
Build or maintain spreadsheets, dashboards, and financial summaries for leadership review.
Support cost analysis, pricing research, revenue assumptions, and financial inputs for business planning.
Assist with procurement comparisons, quote reviews, and budget impact summaries.
Use approved AI-enabled tools, when authorized, to streamline finance templates, summarize information, identify anomalies, and support repeatable analysis while protecting confidential data.
Coordinate with finance, operations, sales, marketing, product, and technical teams to collect accurate information.
Perform other finance, reporting, and business operations support duties as assigned.
Qualifications
Current enrollment in or recent completion of a Finance, Accounting, Business Analytics, Economics, Business Administration, Information Systems, or related degree program.
Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills, including formulas, charts, filters, pivot tables, and organized spreadsheet structure.
Strong attention to detail and ability to work with confidential financial information.
Ability to analyze data, document assumptions, and communicate findings clearly.
Professional communication skills and ability to work with multiple teams.
Preferred Skills
Power BI, Tableau, QuickBooks, ERP, CRM, or budget/reporting tool experience.
Financial modeling, forecasting, cost-benefit analysis, pricing analysis, or revenue tracking exposure.
Python, SQL, or AI-assisted analytics exposure is a plus.
Interest in technology startups, SaaS, investor planning, commercial growth, or government contracting.
What You Will Gain
Practical experience in startup finance, budgeting, procurement, reporting, and financial operations.
Exposure to how finance supports product development, business strategy, and leadership decision-making.
Opportunities to build professional finance work products and strengthen analytical communication skills.
Mentorship and cross-functional collaboration in a technology-focused startup environment.
Ideal Candidate
The ideal candidate is accurate, organized, curious, discreet, and comfortable working with financial data. The candidate should be willing to learn quickly, ask good questions, validate assumptions, and help leadership make informed business decisions.

descriptions.title: Finance Intern Position Description
descriptions.text:
Position Description
Finance Intern

Company: DriverAI
Department: Finance / Business Operations
Reports To: Finance Lead, Chief Financial Officer, or assigned business leader
Employment Type: Internship - Part-Time or Full-Time, based on business need
Work Location: Remote, hybrid, or company-designated location

Position Summary
The Finance Intern supports DriverAI finance, accounting, budgeting, reporting, and business operations activities. This role provides practical exposure to startup finance, financial planning, expense tracking, revenue modeling, budget support, procurement coordination, and internal reporting. The intern will help prepare accurate financial information for leadership decision-making while learning how finance supports product development, business strategy, compliance readiness, investor planning, and operational execution.

Support budget tracking, expense analysis, cash flow summaries, and variance reporting for assigned departments or projects.
Assist with financial data entry, spreadsheet modeling, reconciliation support, invoice tracking, purchase documentation, and payment status monitoring.
Help maintain organized records for expenses, subscriptions, vendors, software tools, equipment purchases, and contract-related financial documentation.
Support development of financial dashboards, budget summaries, burn-rate views, and leadership-ready finance updates using Excel, Power BI, or similar tools.
Assist with revenue, cost, and pricing analysis for products, services, pilots, subscriptions, and customer opportunities.
Support procurement and vendor review by collecting quotes, comparing costs, documenting assumptions, and identifying budget impact.
Help prepare financial inputs for business plans, operating plans, investor materials, grant support, contract support, and project funding requests.
Coordinate with operations, sales, marketing, product, technical teams, and leadership to gather information needed for accurate financial analysis.
Use approved AI-enabled tools, when authorized, to improve finance workflows, summarize financial information, draft templates, identify anomalies, and support repeatable analysis while protecting confidential data.
Maintain confidentiality of company financial information, personnel information, vendor details, pricing, contracts, and intellectual property.
Perform other related finance, business operations, reporting, and administrative duties as assigned.
Required Qualifications
Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Analytics, Economics, Business Administration, Information Systems, or a related field.
Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets, including formulas, charts, filters, pivot tables, and organized spreadsheet design.
Ability to analyze numbers carefully, validate assumptions, and explain findings clearly.
Strong attention to detail, confidentiality, organization, and follow-through.
Ability to communicate professionally with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Willingness to learn startup finance, budgeting, procurement, reporting, and operational planning processes.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with Power BI, Tableau, QuickBooks, ERP systems, CRM systems, accounting systems, or budget management tools.
Exposure to financial modeling, cost-benefit analysis, pricing analysis, forecasting, revenue tracking, or cash flow planning.
Experience using Python, SQL, or AI-assisted analytics tools for finance, data cleaning, reporting, or automation.

Financial accuracy and data integrity
Analytical thinking and practical business judgment
Confidentiality and professional discretion
Clear written and verbal communication
Organization, documentation, and deadline management
Curiosity, accountability, and willingness to learn

Gain hands-on experience with startup budgeting, cost tracking, financial reporting, and operational finance.
Learn how finance supports leadership decisions, product development, investor planning, and contract readiness.
Build stronger financial analysis, spreadsheet modeling, documentation, and communication skills.
Understand how to use AI-enabled tools responsibly for finance workflow support without exposing confidential information.
Develop a portfolio of practical finance work products such as budget trackers, dashboards, cost analyses, and written summaries.
Performance Expectations
Produces accurate, organized, and timely financial work products.
Maintains confidentiality and follows company data handling requirements.
Validates assumptions and escalates unclear or inconsistent information.
Communicates progress, risks, and blockers in a timely manner.
Demonstrates growth in finance, business operations, and analytical capabilities.

descriptions.title: Business Data Analyst Position Description
descriptions.text:
1. Role Purpose / Position Summary
The Business/Data Analyst supports Sales and Marketing with direct involvement from the Data Team to turn business, customer, campaign, product, and operational data into actionable insight. This role develops dashboards, key performance indicators, recurring reports, sales and marketing analytics, data quality checks, and data-driven recommendations that improve lead generation, customer engagement, conversion, retention, revenue growth, product positioning, and leadership decision-making. The position works closely with Sales, Marketing, Data Analytics, Product, Engineering, and leadership stakeholders to define business questions, collect and validate data, analyze performance, and communicate findings clearly.
2. Reporting and Collaboration
Primary Alignment
Supports Sales and Marketing leadership by providing data analysis, reporting, customer insights, campaign performance analysis, market intelligence, and business recommendations.
Works with the Data Team for data sourcing, data definitions, data quality, dashboards, analytics methods, reporting standards, and recurring data products.
Collaborates with Product, Engineering, AWS/cloud, Finance, Operations, and leadership teams when sales, customer, marketing, product usage, or operational data is needed for business decisions.
Maintains a service-oriented analytics approach while ensuring data outputs are accurate, documented, repeatable, and aligned with approved business definitions.
Team Interface
Sales and Marketing: campaign analytics, lead tracking, pipeline reporting, customer segmentation, outreach performance, market research, and revenue-related analysis.
Data Team: data definitions, dashboard design, data quality checks, source validation, query logic, data pipelines, and analytics best practices.
Leadership: executive summaries, key performance indicators, trend analysis, risk/opportunity identification, and decision-support materials.
Technical Teams: application data, product telemetry, customer behavior signals, data integrations, API data, cloud-hosted datasets, and reporting requirements.
3. Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Sales and Marketing Analytics
Analyze sales pipeline, lead generation, conversion rates, campaign performance, customer engagement, market activity, and revenue-related trends.
Develop reporting that helps Sales and Marketing understand which campaigns, channels, customer segments, content, products, and outreach strategies are most effective.
Support customer segmentation, account profiling, buyer behavior analysis, funnel analysis, cohort analysis, market sizing, and competitive or industry research where applicable.
Analyze customer acquisition, retention, churn indicators, engagement patterns, and return on marketing or sales investment.
Provide timely recommendations that help improve targeting, messaging, campaign planning, sales prioritization, and customer relationship management.
Dashboard, KPI, and Reporting Development
Design, build, maintain, and improve dashboards, scorecards, recurring reports, and executive summaries for Sales, Marketing, Data Team, and leadership stakeholders.
Define and document key performance indicators, including business purpose, calculation method, source data, refresh cadence, owner, and interpretation guidance.
Build dashboards using tools such as Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Grafana, Amazon QuickSight, Excel, Google Sheets, or similar platforms.
Ensure dashboards are clear, accurate, visually understandable, and useful for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Maintain dashboard documentation, assumptions, metric definitions, filter logic, and known data limitations.
Data Collection, Validation, and Analysis
Collect, clean, validate, and analyze data from customer relationship management tools, marketing platforms, websites, applications, cloud systems, spreadsheets, databases, APIs, and approved external sources.
Write SQL queries, Python scripts, formulas, or analytical workflows to support repeatable reporting and analysis.
Identify data quality issues, incomplete records, inconsistent definitions, outliers, duplicate records, and source-system limitations.
Work directly with the Data Team to verify data definitions, validate source data, and improve reporting reliability.
Support real-time or near-real-time data feedback loops where business or product decisions require faster visibility.
Business Intelligence and Decision Support
Translate business questions into structured analysis plans and clear deliverables.
Prepare findings, summaries, visuals, and recommendations that help leadership understand opportunities, risks, trends, performance gaps, and resource priorities.
Support product-market fit analysis, customer behavior analysis, sales strategy, marketing strategy, partnership opportunities, and business planning.
Assist with forecasts, scenario analysis, pricing insight, territory analysis, market analysis, and strategic performance reviews when needed.
Communicate complex analysis in a concise and business-focused manner.
Data Governance, Privacy, and Documentation
Follow approved data handling, privacy, confidentiality, access control, and security practices when working with company, customer, prospect, user, and marketing data.
Coordinate with the Data Team and cybersecurity personnel to ensure data use aligns with internal policy, customer obligations, and applicable governance requirements.
Document data sources, metric definitions, query logic, assumptions, dashboard refresh schedules, and analysis methods.
Support data quality improvement, data lineage, access reviews, and audit-support documentation when assigned.
Protect confidential business information, customer information, sales strategy, marketing plans, product data, and intellectual property.
Cross-Functional Support and Other Duties
Participate in planning meetings, data reviews, sales/marketing performance discussions, dashboard reviews, and business strategy sessions.
Collaborate with stakeholders to prioritize analytics requests and clarify scope, data availability, timelines, and expected outcomes.
Support process improvement by identifying opportunities to automate recurring reports, reduce manual data work, and improve decision-making speed.
Provide analysis and reporting support for related business, product, operations, finance, or leadership needs when assigned.
Perform other duties as assigned based on company priorities, business needs, and professional development pathways.
4. Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Business Analytics, Data Analytics, Information Systems, Marketing Analytics, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, Data Science, Business Administration, or a related field; equivalent practical experience may be considered.
Experience analyzing business, sales, marketing, customer, product, or operational data.
Strong proficiency with Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets, including formulas, pivot tables, data cleaning, and structured analysis.
Working knowledge of SQL or demonstrated ability to query, join, filter, and validate structured data.
Experience with dashboards, key performance indicators, reports, charts, and visual storytelling.
Ability to collect data from multiple sources and validate accuracy before presenting conclusions.
Strong critical thinking, problem-solving, written communication, and presentation skills.
Ability to explain findings clearly to sales, marketing, technical, and executive stakeholders.
Strong attention to detail and ability to work independently while collaborating with Data Team and business stakeholders.
5. Preferred Qualifications
Experience with Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Amazon QuickSight, Grafana, Metabase, or similar dashboarding tools.
Experience with Python, R, JavaScript, data scraping, APIs, or basic automation workflows.
Experience with customer relationship management and marketing platforms such as HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, Mailchimp, Google Analytics, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Meta Ads, Google Ads, or similar tools.
Experience supporting sales funnel analysis, lead scoring, campaign analytics, customer segmentation, marketing attribution, or customer retention analysis.
Familiarity with AWS, cloud-hosted datasets, databases, data warehouses, or business intelligence data models.
Exposure to data governance, cybersecurity reporting, privacy requirements, customer data protection, or compliance-driven analytics.
Experience in a startup, technology company, product development environment, or fast-moving sales and marketing organization.
Familiarity with artificial intelligence, machine learning, predictive analytics, customer behavior modeling, or advanced analytics techniques.
6. Tools and Technologies
Analytics and reporting: Excel, Google Sheets, Power BI, Tableau, Looker, QuickSight, Grafana, Metabase, or similar tools.
Data access and analysis: SQL, Python, R, APIs, JSON, spreadsheets, databases, cloud systems, and approved web-based sources.
Sales and marketing systems: CRM, email marketing, campaign management, website analytics, social media analytics, and customer engagement platforms.
Collaboration: Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, GitHub, Jira, Confluence, or similar tools.
Cloud/data platforms: AWS, relational databases, data warehouses, data lakes, or other cloud-hosted data environments as assigned.
7. Core Competencies
Sales and marketing business acumen.
Data-driven decision support.
Critical analysis and problem solving.
Dashboard and KPI development.
Clear communication and executive summarization.
Data quality awareness and documentation discipline.
Collaboration with Data Team and business stakeholders.
Customer, market, and revenue orientation.
Adaptability in a startup or fast-changing environment.
Professional judgment, confidentiality, and accountability.
8. Deliverables and Artifacts
Sales and marketing dashboards, scorecards, and reports.
Key performance indicator definitions and metric dictionaries.
Campaign, funnel, lead, customer, and market analysis summaries.
Customer segmentation, cohort, conversion, retention, and engagement analysis.
Data quality findings, source documentation, and dashboard assumptions.
Executive summaries, slide inputs, recommendations, and business decision-support materials.
Automated reporting templates and recurring analysis workflows.
Documentation for data sources, queries, calculations, and reporting cadence.
9. Performance Measures
Accurate, timely, and business-relevant reporting for Sales, Marketing, Data Team, and leadership stakeholders.
Improved visibility into campaign performance, lead generation, conversion, customer behavior, and sales/marketing outcomes.
Clear, usable dashboards and KPIs that support action, accountability, and strategic decision-making.
Reduced manual reporting effort through automation and repeatable analytics workflows.
Strong data validation, documentation, and alignment with approved metric definitions.
Effective collaboration with Sales, Marketing, Data Team, Product, Engineering, and leadership.
High-quality written analysis that identifies risks, opportunities, trends, and recommended actions.
Protection of confidential company, customer, sales, marketing, and product data.
10. Working Conditions and Requirements
This role may operate in a remote, hybrid, or office-based environment depending on company needs. The position requires extended periods working at a computer, use of collaboration and analytics tools, participation in virtual meetings, and frequent coordination with Sales, Marketing, Data Team, and leadership stakeholders. Priorities may shift based on campaign schedules, business development needs, product changes, customer activity, and company growth objectives.

descriptions.title: AWS Lead Job Announcement
descriptions.text:
About DriverAI
DriverAI is building intelligent technology solutions that combine cloud infrastructure, software development, data analytics, artificial intelligence, computer vision, and product intelligence. Our teams work across AWS infrastructure, mobile and web applications, data pipelines, analytics dashboards, and secure operational environments to support scalable product development and business growth.
About the Role
DriverAI is seeking an AWS Lead to support the configuration, administration, monitoring, documentation, and continuous improvement of our Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud environments. This role provides hands-on cloud support and practical technical leadership for assigned AWS work, helping software, data analytics, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence/machine learning, and product teams operate securely and efficiently in the cloud.
This is a lead-level implementation and coordination role. The AWS Lead will help guide cloud tasks, troubleshoot issues, support Identity and Access Management (IAM), assist with deployment workflows, maintain documentation, and support compliance-related technical controls. This role does not replace senior architecture ownership, security policy ownership, or formal compliance governance authority.
Key Responsibilities
Support configuration, administration, monitoring, and maintenance of AWS environments, including compute, storage, networking, databases, logging, and application platform services.
Work with AWS services such as EC2, S3, IAM, Lambda, CloudWatch, RDS, VPC, Route 53, API Gateway, ECR, ECS/EKS, Athena, Glue, Redshift, DynamoDB, QuickSight, and related services as assigned.
Support IAM activities, including roles, permissions, policies, service accounts, access reviews, least-privilege controls, and environment separation.
Assist with Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) workflows, deployments, container support, cloud permissions, build configurations, and rollback procedures.
Interface with Data Analytics and Data Engineering teams to support AWS-hosted data storage, processing, dashboards, reporting, and analytics workflows.
Support cloud infrastructure for software applications, data pipelines, APIs, databases, telemetry, product usage data, and real-time or near-real-time feedback loops.
Monitor AWS resources for availability, performance, configuration drift, service limits, cost concerns, security issues, and operational health.
Assist with logging, monitoring, encryption, backups, recovery, vulnerability remediation, baseline configuration, and secure cloud deployment practices.
Maintain cloud documentation, diagrams, runbooks, access records, deployment notes, troubleshooting procedures, and audit-support evidence when required.
Coordinate with cybersecurity personnel to implement assigned technical controls supporting SOC 2, Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Level 2, National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)-aligned practices, contractual requirements, and company security expectations.
Support cloud-related incident response, root-cause analysis, corrective action planning, and operational improvement activities.
Perform other related duties as assigned based on company priorities, project requirements, operational needs, and professional development pathways.
Required Skills and Experience
Practical experience supporting AWS cloud services, cloud-hosted applications, infrastructure operations, or technical deployment workflows.
Working knowledge of core AWS services such as EC2, S3, IAM, Lambda, CloudWatch, RDS, VPC, Route 53, API Gateway, and related services.
Understanding of IAM, least privilege, role-based access, environment separation, logging, monitoring, backups, and secure cloud configuration practices.
Experience troubleshooting cloud, application, deployment, networking, storage, database, access, or configuration issues.
Familiarity with Git, issue tracking, documentation tools, and collaborative technical workflows.
Ability to document technical configurations, procedures, risks, findings, and operating instructions clearly.
Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate with software, data, cybersecurity, product, and leadership teams.
Ability to work independently on assigned tasks while following technical direction and escalating risks appropriately.
Preferred Skills
Experience with CI/CD pipelines, Docker, containers, infrastructure as code, Terraform, CloudFormation, or automated deployment practices.
Experience with AWS services such as ECR, ECS/EKS, Athena, Glue, Redshift, DynamoDB, QuickSight, Step Functions, or Systems Manager.
Experience supporting data analytics, data engineering, artificial intelligence/machine learning, computer vision, or product telemetry workloads in AWS.
Familiarity with SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST SP 800-171, ISO 27001, or secure cloud operations.
Familiarity with Microsoft 365, SharePoint, cloud collaboration tools, cybersecurity tools, or enterprise IT environments.
AWS certification, such as AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner, Solutions Architect Associate, SysOps Administrator Associate, Developer Associate, Security Specialty, or equivalent experience.
Ideal Candidate
The ideal candidate is a hands-on cloud professional who can support AWS operations, troubleshoot technical issues, coordinate with multiple teams, document clearly, and help maintain secure and reliable cloud services. The candidate should be comfortable working in a startup environment, supporting cross-functional technical needs, and balancing reliability, security, cost, speed, and operational discipline.
Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Cloud Computing, Information Systems, Software Engineering, Cybersecurity, Data Science, or a related technical field is preferred.
Equivalent practical experience, internships, certifications, portfolio projects, or demonstrated AWS cloud skills may be considered.
Position Type
Full-time, part-time, internship, or contract options may be considered based on candidate qualifications and business needs.

descriptions.title: AWS Lead Position Description
descriptions.text:
AWS Lead
Position Description

1. Role Purpose / Position Summary
The AWS Lead supports the planning, configuration, administration, monitoring, and improvement of DriverAI’s Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud environments and related platform services. This role provides hands-on cloud leadership for assigned AWS tasks, assists with secure cloud operations, supports identity and access management, helps maintain deployment discipline, and coordinates with software, data, cybersecurity, and product teams to keep cloud services reliable, secure, cost-conscious, and aligned with business priorities.
This position is a practical lead role rather than a senior architecture or governance ownership role. The AWS Lead may guide implementation activities, coordinate cloud work, document configurations, troubleshoot issues, and support technical controls; however, final cloud architecture authority, security policy ownership, compliance governance, and risk acceptance remain with designated company leadership, the Chief Technology Officer, the Chief Information Security Officer, or other assigned control owners.
2. Reporting and Accountability
Reports to the Chief Technology Officer, Engineering Lead, or assigned Department Lead based on company structure and project needs.
Supports AWS cloud execution, operational reliability, technical documentation, and implementation of approved cloud standards.
Coordinates with the Chief Information Security Officer and cybersecurity team to implement required security controls and support compliance objectives.
Works with software, data, web, database, artificial intelligence/machine learning, and product teams to ensure AWS services support approved technical requirements.
Escalates material risks, unresolved technical issues, access concerns, cost anomalies, security findings, or production-impacting problems to the appropriate lead or executive.
3. Essential Duties and Responsibilities
A. AWS Cloud Operations and Platform Support
Assist with configuring, administering, monitoring, and maintaining AWS environments, including compute, storage, networking, databases, logging, and application platform services.
Support AWS services such as EC2, S3, IAM, Lambda, CloudWatch, RDS, VPC, Route 53, API Gateway, ECR, ECS/EKS, Athena, Glue, Redshift, DynamoDB, and related services as assigned.
Help maintain reliable cloud environments that support software development, data analytics, artificial intelligence/machine learning, computer vision, cybersecurity, and business operations.
Monitor AWS resources for availability, performance, configuration drift, access issues, service limits, and operational health.
Assist with backup, recovery, resilience, and continuity procedures for AWS-hosted systems and data workflows.
Support cost awareness by reviewing usage, identifying waste, right-sizing resources, and recommending practical optimization actions.
B. Identity, Access, and Environment Support
Support AWS identity and access management activities, including roles, policies, groups, permissions, service accounts, access keys, and role-based access structures.
Implement assigned least-privilege access requirements under direction from the appropriate technical, security, or governance lead.
Assist with onboarding, offboarding, access reviews, and access lifecycle management for AWS users and services.
Support separation of development, testing, staging, and production environments in accordance with approved company practices.
Document access configurations, permission changes, environment boundaries, and privileged access requirements.
C. CI/CD, Deployment, and Configuration Support
Support secure continuous integration and continuous delivery workflows for cloud and application deployments.
Assist developers and technical leads with deployment pipelines, environment variables, cloud permissions, build configurations, container images, and infrastructure dependencies.
Help enforce approved deployment processes, including testing, review, approval, release logging, rollback planning, and production change control.
Support Git-based workflows, branch discipline, pull requests, code review coordination, and release readiness activities as assigned.
Troubleshoot cloud deployment issues involving access, networking, storage, databases, containers, serverless functions, APIs, logging, and application configuration.
D. Data Analytics and Application Infrastructure Support
Interface with Data Analytics and Data Engineering teams to support AWS-hosted data storage, processing, reporting, dashboards, and analytics-ready workflows.
Assist with cloud infrastructure supporting data pipelines, APIs, databases, object storage, telemetry, product usage data, and real-time or near-real-time feedback loops.
Coordinate with software developers, data engineers, and analysts to ensure AWS services support approved application and analytics requirements.
Support secure data movement and integration between AWS services, internal applications, dashboards, databases, and third-party systems.
E. Security, Compliance, and Governance Support
Implement assigned technical controls that support SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST-aligned practices, contractual requirements, and company security requirements when applicable.
Support logging, monitoring, encryption, backup, vulnerability remediation, baseline configuration, and secure cloud deployment practices.
Assist with audit and assessment readiness by maintaining accurate technical documentation, diagrams, screenshots, configuration records, and evidence as requested.
Coordinate with cybersecurity staff to resolve cloud security findings, misconfigurations, excessive permissions, logging gaps, and control implementation issues.
Follow secure cloud practices and escalate suspected security incidents, access concerns, unauthorized changes, or sensitive-data exposure risks promptly.
F. Change, Incident, and Operational Support
Support change and configuration management processes for AWS environments, deployment pipelines, and cloud-hosted services.
Ensure assigned changes are documented, tested, reviewed, approved, and implemented in accordance with company procedures.
Assist with incident response activities related to AWS infrastructure, deployments, access, availability, configuration, performance, or cloud-hosted services.
Participate in troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, corrective action planning, and post-incident documentation.
Develop and maintain standard operating procedures, runbooks, configuration notes, and troubleshooting guides for recurring AWS tasks.
G. Team Coordination and Other Duties
Provide practical guidance and task coordination to developers, analysts, interns, or technical contributors working within AWS-supported environments.
Participate in sprint planning, architecture discussions, technical reviews, cloud readiness assessments, and project status meetings.
Support tool evaluations, proof-of-concept activities, cloud research, vendor coordination, and implementation planning as needed.
Perform other related duties as assigned based on company needs, project priorities, operational requirements, and professional development pathways.
4. Authority and Decision Rights
May recommend AWS configurations, access structures, deployment improvements, monitoring changes, and cost-optimization actions.
May coordinate assigned AWS work and provide implementation guidance to technical contributors.
May pause or escalate deployment or configuration activities that appear to create security, availability, cost, compliance, or production risks.
Does not independently approve final enterprise cloud architecture, security policy, compliance governance, risk acceptance, or production exceptions unless formally delegated by leadership.
5. Explicit Role Boundaries
This role supports and leads assigned AWS implementation activities but does not replace the Chief Technology Officer, Chief Information Security Officer, formal cloud architect, compliance owner, or control owner.
Security policy ownership, compliance governance, and risk acceptance remain with designated leadership and governance personnel.
The AWS Lead executes approved technical controls, documents work, escalates risks, and helps maintain reliable AWS operations.
6. Required Qualifications
3-6+ years of experience in AWS cloud support, cloud engineering, DevOps, systems administration, software deployment, or related technical work; equivalent practical experience may be considered.
Working knowledge of AWS core services, including compute, storage, networking, identity and access management, databases, monitoring, and application hosting.
Experience supporting cloud deployments, troubleshooting, scripting, automation, or operational workflows.
Familiarity with identity and access management, least privilege, environment separation, secure configuration, logging, and monitoring.
Ability to document technical configurations, procedures, issue resolution steps, and operational runbooks.
Strong analytical, communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently on assigned tasks while coordinating with team leads, technical contributors, and leadership.
7. Preferred Qualifications
AWS certification such as AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner, AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate, AWS Certified SysOps Administrator - Associate, AWS Certified Developer - Associate, or equivalent experience.
Experience with AWS services such as EC2, S3, IAM, Lambda, CloudWatch, RDS, VPC, Route 53, API Gateway, ECR, ECS/EKS, DynamoDB, Athena, Glue, Redshift, and QuickSight.
Experience with GitHub, GitLab, CI/CD pipelines, Docker, Terraform, CloudFormation, AWS CDK, or infrastructure-as-code practices.
Experience supporting data analytics, data engineering, artificial intelligence/machine learning, computer vision, mobile applications, or web application infrastructure.
Familiarity with SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST SP 800-171, ISO 27001, or secure cloud operations.
Experience in startup, product development, agile engineering, or cross-disciplinary technical environments.
8. Core Competencies
Hands-on AWS operations and troubleshooting.
Cloud reliability, documentation, and operational discipline.
Secure configuration and least-privilege mindset.
Deployment and environment management support.
Cross-functional collaboration with software, data, cybersecurity, and product teams.
Ability to communicate technical issues clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Adaptability, accountability, and willingness to support evolving startup requirements.
9. Deliverables and Artifacts
AWS configuration documentation, diagrams, and support notes.
IAM role, policy, account, and access documentation.
Deployment and CI/CD support documentation.
Runbooks, standard operating procedures, troubleshooting guides, and escalation notes.
Monitoring, logging, backup, recovery, and cost-review artifacts.
Audit-support evidence, screenshots, configuration records, and technical explanations when requested.
Issue-resolution summaries, post-incident notes, and corrective action support documentation.
10. Performance Measures
Reliable AWS operations with timely identification and escalation of technical issues.
Accurate and current documentation for assigned AWS services, access structures, and operational procedures.
Consistent support for secure access, least privilege, environment separation, and approved deployment practices.
Effective collaboration with engineering, data, cybersecurity, and leadership teams.
Timely completion of assigned AWS tasks, troubleshooting actions, and implementation support activities.
Improved monitoring, automation, cost awareness, and operational efficiency.
Successful support for audits, assessments, evidence collection, and remediation activities when applicable.
11. Work Environment
This role may operate in a remote, hybrid, or office-based environment depending on company needs. The AWS Lead may support multiple projects simultaneously and should be comfortable working in a cross-disciplinary startup environment where priorities may shift based on technical, operational, customer, funding, compliance, or product requirements. The role requires extended periods working at a computer, using cloud consoles and technical collaboration tools, participating in virtual meetings, and supporting occasional urgent operational needs.

descriptions.title: Cloud Database Engineer  PD
descriptions.text:
Job Description- Cloud Database Engineer

Our Cloud Database Engineers will design and manage cloud-based database solutions for performance, security, and availability. Some primary responsibilities are migrating data, automating tasks, optimizing cloud resource usage, ensuring data quality, and collaborating with development teams. They should be able to work with platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud and use tools like SQL, Python, and infrastructure-as-code (IaC) to manage and maintain databases.

Design and implement scalable, highly available database solutions on cloud platforms.
Develop a high-performance RESTful API using Python and FastAPI.
Manage and maintain services: Oversee day-to-day operations, including monitoring, troubleshooting, backup, and disaster recovery.
Migrate and deploy: Plan and execute the migration of data and applications to the cloud, and deploy new databases.
Optimize performance: Tune queries, optimize storage, and implement caching strategies to maximize efficiency and system performance.
Automate tasks: Using scripting languages like Python or shell scripts to automate repetitive tasks
Ensure security and compliance: Implement best practices to maintain security protocols and ensure compliance with data governance policies.
Manage costs: Balance performance needs with cloud resource costs by intelligently scaling and allocating resources.
Collaborate: Work with developers and other engineering teams to align database designs with application requirements. 
Required skills and experience
Cloud platforms: Experience with major cloud providers such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
Database technologies: Proficiency with relational and NoSQL databases (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, MongoDB).
Scripting: Exceptional scripting skills, especially with languages like Python or shell scripting.
Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Manage infrastructure programmatically with tools similar to Terraform or CloudFormation.
Data pipelines: Understanding of data pipeline architecture and ETL/ELT processes.
Performance tuning: Ability to analyze and optimize database performance.
Operating systems: Experience with Linux administration is often required.
CI/CD: Familiarity with CI/CD principles and tools is a plus.

Job Announcement Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)

About the Opportunity
DriverAI is seeking a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) to lead security governance, risk management, compliance oversight, resilience planning, incident governance, third-party security, audit readiness, and executive security advisory functions. The role supports SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST-aligned governance, secure growth, emergency response and continuity planning, AI/data governance, and coordination with technology and corporate security stakeholders while preserving clear separation between security oversight and technical execution.
Position Overview
The CISO defines and matures the information security program, including security strategy, policy, control oversight, risk reporting, incident governance, business continuity and disaster recovery oversight, third-party security, audit readiness, regulatory or contractual reporting support, and executive reporting. The role reports to the Chief Technology Officer (CTO), unless otherwise assigned, and works with engineering, cloud, cybersecurity operations, legal, privacy, product, finance, corporate security, contracting, and executive leadership.
This is a governance and oversight role, not a routine system administration role. Technology execution remains with the CTO and assigned operational owners; the CISO ensures security expectations are defined, validated, monitored, escalated, and improved.
Key Responsibilities
Develop and maintain the enterprise security strategy, roadmap, policies, standards, procedures, control expectations, exception process, and executive reporting cadence.
Establish governance aligned with SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST SP 800-171, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 27001 concepts, customer requirements, privacy obligations, and contractual commitments.
Maintain the security risk register and remediation tracker; report key risks, treatment plans, control gaps, incident trends, resilience findings, and security posture to leadership.
Lead or oversee risk assessments, control evaluations, compliance readiness reviews, customer security responses, audit support, evidence collection, and corrective action tracking.
Develop, maintain, or oversee applicable security governance documents, including the Incident Response Plan, Emergency Response Plan, Business Continuity Plan, Disaster Recovery Plan, Continuity of Operations Plan, escalation matrices, crisis communication procedures, tabletop exercise records, and post-incident improvement plans.
Coordinate breach notification, regulatory reporting, contractual incident reporting, customer notifications, evidence preservation, legal/privacy coordination, and remediation documentation when required.
Define security requirements for identity and access management, encryption, endpoint protection, logging, monitoring, secure configuration, cloud security, network protection, data protection, backup, recovery, and service restoration.
Lead or oversee the evaluation and selection of security applications and platforms that protect the environment from endpoint to network, using documented technical, operational, compliance, integration, vendor-risk, lifecycle, and cost criteria. Validate that selected capabilities support defense in depth, centralized visibility, effective detection and response, secure administration, and measurable risk reduction.
Review cloud, application, data, AI, machine learning, computer vision, mobile, web, and product designs for alignment with approved security and data protection requirements.
Define secure development and DevSecOps expectations for secure coding, code review, dependency management, secrets management, environment separation, production change control, and deployment governance.
Provide governance oversight for managed detection and response, security monitoring, vulnerability management, incident response, security operations metrics, and control effectiveness.
Define and oversee third-party and supply chain security requirements, including vendor due diligence, security contract terms, access restrictions, data protection obligations, and reassessment cadence.
Collaborate with the Corporate Facilities Security Officer (CFSO), Corporate Security, legal, contracting, and executives to align cybersecurity policies with facility security, personnel security, visitor controls, export control, controlled unclassified information (CUI), classified program, DCSA, NATO, customer, and contract security requirements, as applicable.
Define or support AI governance, model and training data protection, data classification, data retention, privacy-by-design, and prevention of intellectual property or sensitive data leakage.
Establish security awareness, role-based training, executive briefings, developer security education, incident reporting awareness, and practical security culture initiatives.
Recommend security investment priorities, risk treatment, exception decisions, and risk acceptance options to executive leadership.
Required Qualifications
Five to ten years of direct experience serving as a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), Deputy CISO, or equivalent executive information security leader with enterprise-wide accountability.
Current Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) certification is required.
Strong enterprise networking background is required, including network architecture, segmentation, routing and switching, firewalls, secure remote access, identity-aware access controls, network monitoring, and defense-in-depth principles.
Proven experience evaluating, selecting, and governing security applications is required, including establishing documented selection criteria based on risk, security effectiveness, interoperability, scalability, manageability, compliance, cost, vendor support, and total cost of ownership. Experience must span layered protection from endpoints through identity, email, cloud, applications, data, network infrastructure, monitoring, detection, response, and recovery capabilities.
Proven experience leading and developing cybersecurity, information security, governance, risk, compliance, or related technical teams is required, including assigning priorities, establishing accountability, mentoring personnel, and delivering measurable results.
Demonstrated experience with SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST SP 800-171, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 27001, or similar frameworks.
Strong background in security governance, risk management, audit readiness, policy development, incident governance, resilience planning, vendor risk, and compliance oversight.
Ability to translate security and compliance requirements into clear policies, practical procedures, control expectations, remediation plans, continuity expectations, and measurable outcomes.
Strong executive communication and writing skills for risk briefings, board or executive reports, policies, audit responses, incident documentation, customer assurance materials, and governance records.
Ability to collaborate effectively with CTO, engineering, cloud, cybersecurity operations, product, legal, privacy, finance, contracting, corporate security, and business stakeholders.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience leading geographically dispersed or remote teams across multiple time zones is preferred, including effective communication, coordination, performance management, and continuity of operations across distributed work environments.
Experience in a startup, technology, cloud, software, AI, computer vision, SaaS, federal contracting, defense, government, international, or regulated environment.
Experience with SOC 2 readiness, CMMC Level 2 readiness, NIST SP 800-171 implementation, customer security reviews, DCSA/NATO/customer security expectations, or compliance automation.
Cloud security experience is optional. Familiarity with AWS, Microsoft 365, Entra ID, endpoint detection and response, managed detection and response, vulnerability management, security information and event management, governance, risk, and compliance platforms, or compliance automation tools is beneficial.
Additional certifications, such as CISM, CISA, CRISC, CCSP, Security+, or vendor-specific cloud security credentials, are optional and may be considered beneficial.
Experience advising secure development, DevSecOps, product security, privacy-by-design, AI governance, data governance, third-party risk, business continuity, disaster recovery, or incident response programs.
Authority and Role Boundaries
The CISO defines and enforces security policy, standards, governance expectations, procedures, and control requirements.
The CISO may require remediation plans and escalate material security risks, continuity risks, incident reporting concerns, exceptions, or unresolved control gaps.
The CISO recommends risk treatment and risk acceptance decisions; final risk acceptance remains with executive leadership or the designated business risk owner.
The CISO does not own technology infrastructure, production systems, application operations, or routine system administration; execution remains with the CTO and designated technical teams.
Ideal Candidate
The ideal candidate is a practical, business-minded security leader who can build structure without slowing innovation. They understand compliance frameworks without treating compliance as a paperwork exercise; communicate risks in plain language; build trust with technical, corporate security, and executive stakeholders; and support product delivery, customer trust, government or regulated opportunities, and long-term scalability.
What Success Looks Like
Security governance is documented, approved, maintained, understood by responsible owners, and supported by disciplined evidence.
Risk register, remediation tracker, incident reporting process, continuity findings, and executive reports provide clear visibility into priorities.
SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST, customer assurance, and audit readiness activities are organized and evidence-driven.
Incident response, emergency response, business continuity, disaster recovery, continuity of operations, escalation procedures, tabletop exercises, and post-incident improvements are documented and maintained.
Security requirements are integrated into cloud, product, software development, vendor, AI/data, corporate security, incident response, and business workflows.
Material risks are escalated early, tracked to closure, and supported by informed risk acceptance decisions.
Security culture improves through practical training, clear procedures, role-based expectations, and cross-functional collaboration.
Education, Work Environment, and Application Materials
Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Risk Management, Business, or a related field preferred. A master’s degree, relevant certifications, military/government security experience, federal contracting experience, corporate security coordination experience, or equivalent executive security leadership experience may be considered.
Full-time, fractional, advisory, or contract options may be considered based on company needs and candidate qualifications. Work may be remote, hybrid, or at a company-designated location. Periodic after-hours support may be required for significant incidents, emergency response coordination, customer requirements, audits, tabletop exercises, or executive briefings.
Applicants should provide a resume or curriculum vitae and a brief statement describing relevant security governance, risk, compliance, incident response, resilience, and executive leadership experience. Non-confidential examples of frameworks, audits, compliance programs, business continuity or incident response programs, or security governance initiatives may be included.

The role supports SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST-aligned governance, secure product growth, emergency response and continuity planning, CFSO/corporate security coordination, AI/data governance, and clear separation between security oversight and technology execution.

Ensure sensitive company, customer, government, contract, and proprietary information is protected when using cloud services, internal AI tools, external AI tools, development environments, collaboration platforms, and third-party services.
K. Training, Awareness, and Security Culture
Establish and oversee security awareness, phishing awareness, role-based security training, executive security briefings, developer security education, incident reporting awareness, and data handling guidance.
Promote a security-first culture that balances risk management, operational practicality, customer trust, product delivery, and business growth.
Ensure security guidance is understandable, actionable, and translated into procedures, checklists, templates, and role-specific expectations.
4. Authority and Decision Rights
Authority to define, maintain, and enforce enterprise information security policies, standards, procedures, and control expectations.
Authority to require remediation plans for identified security control gaps, audit findings, critical vulnerabilities, material risk issues, and incident or resilience findings.
Authority to escalate material security risks, compliance concerns, security exceptions, incident reporting concerns, continuity risks, and unresolved remediation issues to executive leadership.
Authority to recommend risk treatment, risk acceptance, tool selection priorities, resilience priorities, and security investment needs; final budget and risk acceptance approvals remain with executive leadership.
Authority to pause or recommend pausing activities that create unacceptable security, compliance, contractual, customer, regulatory, or operational resilience risk pending executive review.
5. Explicit Role Boundaries
The CISO does not own technology infrastructure, application operations, production systems, or day-to-day system administration.
The CISO does not perform routine engineering, cloud administration, help desk, or application development tasks unless specifically assigned on an interim basis.
The CISO does not replace formally assigned SOC 2, CMMC, NIST, privacy, business, technical, or corporate security control owners.
The CISO defines governance requirements and oversight expectations; implementation is performed by designated technology, engineering, cybersecurity operations, corporate security, or business owners.
The CISO recommends risk decisions; final risk acceptance belongs to executive leadership or the designated business risk owner.
6. Required Qualifications
Five to ten years of direct experience serving as a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), Deputy CISO, or equivalent executive information security leader with enterprise-wide accountability.
Current Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) certification is required.
Strong enterprise networking background is required, including network architecture, segmentation, routing and switching, firewalls, secure remote access, identity-aware access controls, network monitoring, and defense-in-depth principles.
Proven experience evaluating, selecting, and governing security applications is required, including establishing documented selection criteria based on risk, security effectiveness, interoperability, scalability, manageability, compliance, cost, vendor support, and total cost of ownership. Experience must span layered protection from endpoints through identity, email, cloud, applications, data, network infrastructure, monitoring, detection, response, and recovery capabilities.
Proven experience leading and developing cybersecurity, information security, governance, risk, compliance, or related technical teams is required, including assigning priorities, establishing accountability, mentoring personnel, and delivering measurable results.
Demonstrated experience building or operating security governance programs aligned with SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST, ISO 27001, or similar frameworks.
Strong understanding of information security governance, risk management, audit readiness, security policies, incident response governance, resilience planning, identity and access management, cloud security, vendor risk, and data protection.
Ability to communicate security risks clearly to executive, technical, business, legal, audit, customer, contracting, and corporate security stakeholders.
Experience leading cross-functional security initiatives, coordinating remediation, and converting framework requirements into practical operating procedures.
Strong written communication skills for policies, executive briefings, board updates, control narratives, risk registers, audit responses, incident documentation, and security governance records.
7. Preferred Qualifications
Experience leading geographically dispersed or remote teams across multiple time zones is preferred, including effective communication, coordination, performance management, and continuity of operations across distributed work environments.
Experience in a startup, technology company, artificial intelligence, computer vision, cloud, SaaS, defense, federal contracting, government, international, or regulated environment.
Experience supporting SOC 2 readiness, CMMC Level 2 readiness, NIST SP 800-171 control implementation, FedRAMP-aligned cloud considerations, customer security due diligence, or DCSA/NATO/customer security expectations.
Cloud security experience is optional, but familiar with Amazon Web Services, Microsoft 365, Entra ID, endpoint detection and response, managed detection and response, vulnerability management, security information and event management, governance, risk, and compliance platforms, or compliance automation tools is beneficial.
Additional certifications, such as CISM, CISA, CRISC, CCSP, Security+, or vendor-specific cloud security credentials, are optional and may be considered beneficial.
Experience advising secure development, DevSecOps, artificial intelligence governance, data governance, privacy-by-design, product security, business continuity, disaster recovery, or incident response programs.
8. Core Competencies
Executive judgment and ethical leadership.
Security governance and risk-based decision support.
Clear separation of oversight, ownership, and execution.
Audit readiness and evidence discipline.
Strategic planning and practical implementation guidance.
Incident governance, emergency response, and crisis coordination.
Business continuity, disaster recovery, and resilience awareness.
Cross-functional collaboration with technology, legal, privacy, contracting, CFSO/corporate security, and business stakeholders.
Clear, concise technical and executive communication.
Continuous improvement and measurable control maturity.
9. Deliverables and Artifacts
Enterprise security strategy, roadmap, and annual program priorities.
Security policies, standards, procedures, exception process, and review cadence.
Risk register, control maturity assessment, remediation tracker, and executive risk reports.
SOC 2, CMMC, NIST, customer assurance, and audit readiness documentation.
Incident Response Plan, Emergency Response Plan, Business Continuity Plan, Disaster Recovery Plan, Continuity of Operations Plan, crisis communication procedures, escalation matrix, tabletop exercise records, and post-incident review templates.
Vendor security assessment criteria, third-party risk records, supply chain risk inputs, and security contract requirement inputs.
Security application evaluation criteria, comparative assessments, selection recommendations, implementation governance requirements, and lifecycle review records covering endpoint, identity, email, cloud, application, data, network, monitoring, detection, response, and recovery technologies.
AI/data governance security requirements, privacy-by-design inputs, and sensitive data leakage prevention guidance.
Security awareness plan, role-based training requirements, developer security education requirements, and reporting metrics.
10. Performance Measures
Strong audit and assessment outcomes with minimal repeat findings.
Documented security governance program with clear policy ownership, control ownership, evidence standards, and review cadence.
Measurable reduction in high-priority security risks, aged remediation items, unresolved control gaps, and repeat incident findings.
Timely executive risk reporting and informed risk acceptance decisions.
Effective incident governance, coordinated communication, required reporting support, and completed post-incident remediation tracking.
Documented and tested emergency response, continuity, disaster recovery, escalation, and tabletop exercise processes.
Security requirements incorporated into product, cloud, development, AI/data, vendor, contracting, corporate security, and business processes without unnecessary operational disruption.
Positive collaboration with CTO, technical teams, legal, privacy, CFSO/corporate security, contracting, business leadership, and customers.
11. Working Conditions and Requirements
Extended periods working at a computer and using cloud, collaboration, governance, documentation, and security tools.
Participation in executive meetings, audit reviews, incident response discussions, emergency response planning, customer assurance activities, tabletop exercises, and periodic after-hours incident coordination when necessary.
Must protect confidential company information, customer information, security documentation, audit evidence, intellectual property, system data, controlled information when applicable, and sensitive business records.
Perform other duties as assigned that are consistent with the scope, seniority, and governance responsibilities of the position.

Corporate Facilities Security Officer
Job Announcement

Company: DriverAI
Position Title: Corporate Facilities Security Officer (CFSO)
Position Type: Full-Time, Part-Time, Consultant, or Contract, depending on candidate qualifications and business needs
Location: Remote, hybrid, office, customer site, or secure facility location based on operational requirements
Reports To: CEO, President/COO, or designated executive
Application: Send resume and relevant security/government contracting experience to Apply@DriverAI.io
About DriverAI
DriverAI is building advanced technology capabilities that combine artificial intelligence, computer vision, precision navigation, cloud platforms, and secure operations. As the company expands into commercial, government, international, and potentially classified or controlled work, we require disciplined security leadership that can protect the business while enabling growth, partnerships, and contract execution.
About the Role
DriverAI is seeking a Corporate Facilities Security Officer (CFSO) to lead facility security, industrial security, physical security, visitor control, emergency planning, contract security support, and international security governance. This is a strategic and operational role. The CFSO will help executives and Contracting Officers understand security requirements before the company enters contracts, operations agreements, partnerships, facility commitments, NATO-related opportunities, foreign-government engagements, or classified/controlled work.
The ideal candidate can operate across business strategy, facilities, contracts, DCSA/NISPOM readiness, NATO or allied security expectations, foreign-country requirements, physical security, personnel security, emergency response, and coordination with the CTO and CISO. The candidate must be able to convert complex security obligations into clear business recommendations, executable procedures, and audit-ready documentation.
Key Responsibilities
Develop and maintain the corporate facility security governance framework, including facility security plans, physical security procedures, visitor control, access control, emergency response, continuity of operations, incident reporting, and security training documents.
Advise the CEO, President/COO, CTO, CISO, Contracting Officers, Program Managers, and operations leaders on security obligations, facility impacts, risks, cost drivers, schedule impacts, staffing needs, and decision options.
Review contracts, solicitations, operations agreements, teaming agreements, security clauses, statements of work, contract security classification guidance, subcontractor requirements, and foreign partnership arrangements for security impact.
Support readiness for DCSA engagement, facility clearance considerations, National Industrial Security Program requirements, personnel security support, visit authorizations, self-inspections, security training, and audit documentation when applicable.
Assess NATO, allied, coalition, host-nation, and foreign-government security requirements, including handling, access, visitor, storage, releasability, subcontractor, and facility obligations when applicable.
Develop and enforce physical security controls for offices, labs, secure rooms, network/server areas, equipment storage, project spaces, reception areas, and restricted-access work areas.
Manage visitor control, badging, access authorization, escort procedures, foreign national visits, government/customer visits, vendor access, emergency access, and removal of company property.
Coordinate with the CISO on controlled unclassified information, classified/controlled information boundaries, incident response, cyber/physical incident coordination, data protection, and security governance.
Coordinate with the CTO on facility, technical, network, cloud, communications, classified/controlled workspace, secure storage, monitoring, and infrastructure requirements before architecture or operational decisions are finalized.
Support foreign ownership/control/influence awareness, foreign access reviews, foreign travel coordination, foreign partnership risk reviews, export control coordination, and supply chain security escalation.
Create executive-ready decision memos, security risk assessments, compliance matrices, corrective action plans, training records, incident records, visitor logs, inspection records, and security implementation plans.
Lead or support audits, customer reviews, government inspections, internal self-assessments, incident reviews, emergency drills, and lessons-learned updates.
Required Qualifications
Experience in corporate security, facility security, physical security, industrial security, government contracting, classified contract support, military security, law enforcement security operations, or similar security discipline.
Ability to interpret security requirements and translate them into operational plans, procedures, staffing needs, facility requirements, and executive recommendations.
Experience with access control, visitor management, emergency procedures, incident reporting, documentation, security training, and facility risk assessment.
Strong writing and briefing skills, including ability to prepare policies, procedures, decision memos, security plans, checklists, and leadership summaries.
Ability to work with executives, contracting personnel, technical teams, cybersecurity staff, facilities teams, vendors, subcontractors, customers, and government representatives.
Sound judgment, discretion, confidentiality, and ability to protect sensitive company, customer, government, contract, personnel, and proprietary information.
Preferred Qualifications
Prior experience as a Facility Security Officer, Assistant Facility Security Officer, Contractor Program Security Officer, Corporate Security Officer, Physical Security Manager, Industrial Security Specialist, or government/military security lead.
Familiarity with DCSA, facility clearance processes, NISPOM/32 CFR Part 117, personnel security, visit authorization systems, self-inspection requirements, and industrial security training expectations.
Familiarity with NATO security requirements, classified project and industrial security concepts, foreign-government security requirements, host-nation requirements, and allied/coalition contract environments.
Experience supporting contracts involving classified information, controlled unclassified information, export-controlled data, defense customers, intelligence customers, NATO customers, foreign governments, or overseas facilities.
Experience coordinating with cybersecurity programs involving CMMC Level 2, NIST SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-53, SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, incident response, and continuity planning.
Security certifications, CDSE training, Physical Security Professional, Certified Protection Professional, Security Fundamentals Professional Certification, Industrial Security Professional, Security+, or equivalent training/experience.
What Success Looks Like
Leadership receives timely, clear, and actionable security advice before business commitments are made.
Security requirements are built into proposals, contracts, operations agreements, facility plans, technical plans, and project execution plans early enough to avoid rework.
Facility access, visitor management, foreign national visits, emergency response, incident reporting, and controlled information processes are documented and consistently executed.
DCSA, NATO, foreign-country, customer, and contract security obligations are identified, tracked, implemented, and auditable when applicable.
The CFSO enables business growth while reducing avoidable security, compliance, contractual, foreign disclosure, and operational risk.
Ideal Candidate
The ideal candidate is a practical, detail-oriented security professional who can work at both the executive and operational levels. The candidate understands that security must protect the company and enable the mission. They can brief leaders, coordinate with technical teams, draft procedures, review contracts, manage facility controls, support government requirements, and build repeatable security processes that scale with the company.
Position Details
Employment status and work location will be based on business need, contract requirements, and candidate qualifications.
Some assignments may require U.S. citizenship, background investigation, security clearance eligibility, nondisclosure agreements, foreign travel reporting, customer approval, or government authorization.
Some work may require travel to company offices, customer sites, government sites, partner facilities, or overseas locations.
DriverAI may adjust duties based on contract requirements, government direction, facility status, program priorities, and company growth.
How to Apply
Please send your resume and a short summary of relevant facility security, industrial security, government contracting, NATO/international security, physical security, or emergency management experience to Apply@DriverAI.io.
