descriptions.title: Corporate Facilities Security Officer Position Description
descriptions.text:
Corporate Facilities Security Officer
Position Description

Company: DriverAI
Position Title: Corporate Facilities Security Officer (CFSO)
Department: Security / Facilities / Corporate Operations
Reports To: Chief Executive Officer (CEO), President/Chief Operating Officer (COO), or designated executive
Key Interfaces: CEO, President/COO, Chief Technology Officer (CTO), Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), Contracting Officers, Program Managers, Legal/Compliance Advisors, Facility Leadership, Security Vendors, and Government Security Representatives
Employment Type: Full-Time, Part-Time, Consultant, or Contract, as assigned
Work Location: Remote, hybrid, office, or secure facility location based on operational and contract requirements
Version / Effective Date: Draft v1.0 / May 2026
1. Role Purpose and Position Summary
Bottom Line Up Front: The Corporate Facilities Security Officer (CFSO) establishes, operates, and continuously improves DriverAI's corporate facility, industrial security, physical security, contract security, and international security governance program. This position ensures company facilities, personnel, operations, classified or controlled workspaces, visitor controls, foreign national processes, emergency programs, and contract security obligations are aligned with applicable U.S. government, NATO, foreign-country, customer, and business requirements.
The CFSO is a senior operational security advisor. The role supports executive decision-making by identifying security requirements, contract obligations, facility risks, foreign ownership/control/influence considerations, operational constraints, and implementation costs so the CEO, President/COO, CTO, CISO, Contracting Officers, and Program Managers can make informed business, technical, contractual, and operational decisions before commitments are made.
2. Reporting, Accountability, and Decision Support
Reports to the CEO, President/COO, or designated executive, with routine coordination across the CTO, CISO, program, contracting, legal, facilities, and operations teams.
Serves as the company focal point for facility security, industrial security, physical security, government security interface, visitor control, classified/controlled facility operations, and contract security execution.
Advises leadership before contract proposal submission, contract award acceptance, teaming agreement execution, foreign-partner engagement, facility buildout, classified work start, or operational change that may create security obligations.
Provides written risk, cost, staffing, timeline, facilities, foreign disclosure, and compliance considerations to support executive, contracting, and operational decisions.
Coordinates with the CISO on cyber, information security, incident response, data governance, controlled unclassified information, classified system boundaries, and technology implementation requirements.
Coordinates with the CTO to ensure facility, physical, environmental, communications, cloud, network, and classified/controlled workspace requirements are understood before technical architecture decisions are finalized.
Coordinates with Contracting Officers and Program Managers to review contract security clauses, security classification guidance, deliverable controls, reporting obligations, visitor requirements, and flow-down obligations to subcontractors.
3. Essential Duties and Responsibilities
A. Corporate Facility Security Governance
Develop, maintain, and enforce a corporate facility security governance framework covering physical security, visitor control, access authorization, secure areas, property protection, security training, incident reporting, recordkeeping, and audit readiness.
Develop or maintain applicable documents, including Facility Security Plan, Corporate Security Plan, Physical Security Plan, Visitor Control Plan, Badge and Access Control Procedure, Foreign National Visitor Procedure, Security Education and Training Plan, Emergency Action Plan, Continuity of Operations Plan, Incident Reporting Procedure, Security Self-Inspection Checklist, and Corrective Action Plan templates.
Define security responsibilities for offices, labs, remote work, hybrid work, leased spaces, customer sites, subcontractor locations, secure rooms, storage areas, and special project areas.
Ensure facility security requirements are practical, enforceable, documented, and aligned with business operations, startup realities, customer expectations, and contractual obligations.
B. DCSA, NISPOM, and Cleared Contractor Support
Support company readiness for Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) engagement, facility clearance activities, National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM) compliance, and other cognizant security authority requirements when applicable.
If designated by senior management and eligible, perform Facility Security Officer duties for cleared work, or coordinate with the appointed Facility Security Officer to ensure industrial security execution meets written appointment, training, reporting, and oversight requirements.
Support personnel security processes, visit authorizations, need-to-know validation, classified visit coordination, derivative classification awareness, access records, security briefings, debriefings, and adverse information reporting coordination when applicable.
Maintain or coordinate required security records, self-inspections, vulnerability remediation, security training evidence, government correspondence, and audit-ready documentation.
Coordinate with DCSA Industrial Security Representatives or other government security officials on facility changes, classified contract execution, reporting events, compliance questions, and corrective actions.
C. NATO, Allied, and Foreign-Government Security Requirements
Assess NATO, allied, coalition, and foreign-government security requirements when company opportunities involve NATO information, foreign ministries, defense organizations, foreign military sales, host-nation facilities, foreign subcontractors, or overseas operations.
Identify handling, storage, transmission, visitor, personnel access, marking, releasability, subcontractor, facility, and inspection requirements for NATO classified information or NATO Restricted information when applicable.
Coordinate with U.S. government sponsors, national security authorities, NATO program offices, customer security authorities, and contracting officials to determine which security standards apply to each project, country, and classification level.
Ensure the company does not assume authority to receive, generate, store, transmit, or release NATO, foreign-government, or classified information unless written authorization, contract direction, accreditation, facility clearance, need-to-know, and approved procedures are in place.
Develop country-specific security guidance for foreign operations, including host-nation legal requirements, data protection, export controls, local labor and visitor constraints, secure logistics, facility requirements, secure transportation, and emergency reporting channels.
D. Contract, Proposal, and Operations Agreement Review
Review solicitations, statements of work, security classification specifications, contract data requirements, nondisclosure provisions, facility clauses, flow-down clauses, operational agreements, teaming agreements, subcontractor agreements, memoranda of understanding, and customer security requirements for security impact.
Advise Contracting Officers, executives, and program leaders on whether the company has the facility, personnel, technology, governance, documentation, clearance, export control, and compliance readiness needed to perform contract obligations.
Identify contract risks related to classified work, controlled unclassified information, NATO information, foreign disclosure, foreign ownership/control/influence, subcontractor access, export-controlled data, secure communications, foreign travel, and customer-site operations.
Prepare security inputs for proposal responses, compliance matrices, operations agreements, implementation plans, staffing estimates, facility buildout assumptions, subcontractor management plans, and cost estimates.
Track security obligations from proposal through award, transition, performance, closeout, record retention, and lessons learned.
E. Physical Security, Facilities, Access Control, and Visitor Management
Design and manage physical security controls for offices, labs, secure work areas, equipment areas, server/network spaces, storage rooms, and restricted project areas.
Oversee access control, badges, visitor logs, escort requirements, key and credential management, camera systems, alarms, locks, intrusion detection, security patrols, reception procedures, and after-hours access rules.
Develop and enforce procedures for employee access, vendor access, contractor access, foreign national visits, government customer visits, emergency access, maintenance visits, deliveries, and removal of company property.
Conduct facility risk assessments, vulnerability reviews, security walkthroughs, corrective action tracking, and periodic self-inspections.
Coordinate with landlords, building management, security vendors, facilities teams, and government/customer representatives to ensure facility controls meet operational and contractual needs.
F. Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence, Foreign Engagement, and Supply Chain Coordination
Support identification, documentation, and escalation of Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) risk factors, beneficial ownership concerns, foreign affiliations, foreign financing, foreign board/control issues, foreign contracts, and foreign access requests.
Coordinate with executive leadership, legal counsel, contracting, and government security officials to ensure FOCI-related information is evaluated before transactions, partnerships, foreign investments, subcontracting, or foreign operations are finalized.
Advise on foreign national access, foreign travel, foreign customer engagement, export control coordination, and supply chain security risks affecting classified, controlled, defense, NATO, or sensitive commercial work.
Maintain procedures for reporting, review, mitigation, and documentation of foreign engagement risks when required by contract, law, regulation, or government security direction.
G. Emergency Response, Continuity of Operations, and Incident Coordination
Develop or maintain Emergency Response Plans, Emergency Action Plans, Continuity of Operations Plans, evacuation procedures, shelter-in-place procedures, emergency communications plans, severe weather procedures, workplace violence procedures, and business continuity playbooks.
Coordinate with the CISO to align physical security incidents, cyber incidents, insider threats, data compromise events, emergency reporting, and incident response plans so leadership has a single coordinated operating picture.
Support incident identification, containment, reporting, documentation, escalation, corrective action, and post-incident lessons learned for facility, visitor, theft, loss, unauthorized access, suspicious contact, foreign contact, emergency, or contract security incidents.
Ensure reporting timelines, responsible officials, evidence preservation requirements, government notification channels, customer notification obligations, and legal/compliance review steps are documented.
H. Executive Advisory, Business Strategy, and Operational Decision Support
Provide security impact assessments to leadership for new markets, foreign partnerships, classified opportunities, NATO opportunities, overseas facilities, government proposals, mergers/acquisitions, investment discussions, facility leases, technology deployments, and subcontractor arrangements.
Translate security requirements into business terms, including cost, schedule, staffing, facility buildout, accreditation, licensing, insurance, legal review, and operational constraints.
Participate in executive planning, contract gate reviews, risk reviews, program reviews, and operations planning to ensure security requirements are considered before commitments are made.
Provide clear recommendations that identify required approvals, unresolved risks, decision options, responsible owners, and potential consequences of accepting, mitigating, transferring, or avoiding security risk.
I. Training, Awareness, Audits, and Documentation
Develop and deliver security briefings, visitor handling training, foreign travel guidance, facility security awareness, emergency response training, insider-threat awareness, controlled information handling guidance, and project-specific security briefings.
Maintain evidence of training, acknowledgments, inspection results, incident reports, corrective actions, access reviews, visitor records, and policy approvals.
Lead or support internal assessments, customer audits, government inspections, compliance reviews, and management reviews.
Convert audit findings, incident lessons learned, and customer feedback into updated procedures, training, controls, and management actions.
4. Required Qualifications
Experience in physical security, industrial security, facility security, corporate security, military security, government contracting, classified contract support, or similar operational security discipline.
Working knowledge of facility access control, visitor management, emergency response, incident reporting, security documentation, and security training practices.
Ability to interpret contract security requirements, customer requirements, policies, procedures, and operational constraints and convert them into executable controls.
Strong written communication skills with ability to draft policies, procedures, briefings, decision memos, security plans, and executive recommendations.
Strong judgment, discretion, professionalism, and ability to protect sensitive company, customer, personnel, contract, and government information.
Ability to coordinate across executives, technical teams, cybersecurity, facilities, contracting, legal, vendors, subcontractors, and government/customer representatives.
5. Preferred Qualifications
Prior Facility Security Officer, Assistant Facility Security Officer, Contractor Program Security Officer, Corporate Security Officer, military security manager, government security specialist, or equivalent experience.
Familiarity with DCSA, National Industrial Security Program requirements, NISPOM/32 CFR Part 117, facility clearance processes, personnel security, visit authorization systems, self-inspections, and security training requirements.
Familiarity with NATO security requirements, foreign-government security requirements, host-nation requirements, export controls, International Traffic in Arms Regulations, Export Administration Regulations, and foreign disclosure coordination.
Experience supporting contracts involving classified information, controlled unclassified information, NATO information, defense customers, intelligence community customers, foreign governments, or overseas facilities.
Experience coordinating with cybersecurity leadership on CMMC Level 2, NIST SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-53, SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, incident response, and continuity planning.
Security certifications or training such as CDSE FSO Program Management for Possessing or Non-Possessing Facilities, Security Fundamentals Professional Certification, Industrial Security Professional, Physical Security Professional, Certified Protection Professional, Security+, or equivalent experience.
6. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Industrial security and facility security program management.
Contract security review and executive decision support.
Physical security control design, access control, visitor management, and secure area procedures.
NATO, allied, foreign-government, host-nation, and customer-specific security requirement awareness.
Emergency response, continuity of operations, incident reporting, and corrective action tracking.
FOCI awareness, foreign engagement risk assessment, and escalation discipline.
Clear documentation, briefing, training, and cross-functional coordination.
Ability to balance mission enablement, business strategy, security risk, compliance, and operational practicality.
7. Authority, Role Boundaries, and Escalation
Authority to recommend facility security standards, visitor controls, access restrictions, security documentation requirements, emergency procedures, and corrective actions.
Authority to escalate unresolved facility, contract, classified, foreign access, visitor, emergency, or security compliance risks to executive leadership and the appropriate government/customer security channels.
Authority to pause or recommend suspension of facility access, visits, project activities, or uncontrolled release of sensitive information when security requirements are not met or written authorization is absent.
Does not replace the CISO for cyber governance, information security policy ownership, system authorization, or cyber risk acceptance unless explicitly assigned.
Does not replace the Contracting Officer, legal counsel, export control officer, government security authority, or executive risk acceptance authority.
Provides security recommendations and decision support; final business, legal, contractual, and risk acceptance decisions remain with designated company or government authorities.
8. Performance Measures
Security requirements are identified early enough to inform proposals, contracts, facility planning, technical architecture, and executive decisions.
Facility security documentation is current, enforceable, accessible to authorized personnel, and aligned with applicable contracts and customer requirements.
Visitor, access control, foreign national, emergency, and incident procedures are consistently implemented and auditable.
DCSA, NATO, foreign-government, host-nation, customer, and contractual requirements are tracked and translated into operational controls where applicable.
Executives, Contracting Officers, CTO, CISO, and Program Managers receive timely written security advice with clear decision options and risk implications.
Audits, inspections, self-assessments, and corrective actions are completed on time with evidence maintained.
Incidents, suspicious contacts, access issues, emergency events, and compliance gaps are documented, escalated, remediated, and reviewed for lessons learned.
9. Work Environment and Special Requirements
May require access to sensitive company, customer, government, controlled unclassified, export-controlled, NATO, or classified information depending on contract requirements and eligibility.
May require U.S. citizenship, personnel security clearance eligibility, background investigation, security training, nondisclosure agreements, foreign travel reporting, or customer-specific authorization depending on assigned work.
May require periodic travel to company facilities, customer sites, government facilities, partner facilities, or overseas locations.
May require after-hours support for emergencies, security incidents, facility alarms, customer requirements, or executive decision support.
Reference Sources Used for Governance Alignment
32 Code of Federal Regulations Part 117, National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM), eCFR.
Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA), 32 CFR Part 117 NISPOM Rule and National Industrial Security Program oversight resources.
DCSA Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) guidance and FOCI action planning resources.
Center for Development of Security Excellence (CDSE), Facility Security Officer Toolkit and industrial security training resources.
NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA), procurement terms and conditions and classified project and industrial security directive references.
Applicable contract security requirements, DD Form 254 or equivalent contract security classification guidance, host-nation security law, export control requirements, and customer-specific security clauses.

descriptions.title: CTO Position
descriptions.text:
1. Role Summary
The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is the executive responsible for technology strategy, architecture, and execution across the organization. The CTO ensures that technology platforms are scalable, reliable, secure-by-design, and compliant with regulatory and contractual requirements, including SOC 2 and CMMC Level 2. The CTO serves as the system owner for technology platforms and works in close partnership with the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). While the CTO enables and implements security requirements, cybersecurity policy ownership and the security risk acceptance process remain with the CISO; final risk acceptance decisions reside with other executive leaders.
2. Technology Strategy & Architecture
- The CTO is the final authority for all network architecture, segmentation, connectivity, and routing decisions, including cloud and hybrid environments.
- Define and maintain the enterprise technology roadmap aligned with business objectives and product strategy.
- Establish architectural standards for cloud, application, data, and infrastructure platforms.
- Govern technical debt, lifecycle planning, and platform modernization to support scalability and resilience.
3. Infrastructure, Cloud & Platform Ownership
- Serve as system owner for all production and non-production technology platforms.
- Design and oversee cloud and hybrid infrastructure environments.
- Ensure infrastructure documentation, backups, availability, and recovery capabilities are implemented and maintained.
- Ensure that infrastructure design and operations support defined business continuity and disaster recovery objectives.
4. Engineering & DevSecOps Governance
- Establish and govern software development lifecycle (SDLC) and CI/CD standards.
- Enforce secure development, testing, and release practices.
- Ensure all system changes are reviewed, tested, approved, and auditable.
5. Security Alignment & Compliance Enablement
- Security requirements are implemented according to policies defined by security leadership.
- Partner with the CISO to ensure technology platforms meet defined security requirements.
- Implement technical controls supporting access control, logging, monitoring, encryption, and configuration baselines.
- Support audit readiness by ensuring system documentation and evidence are accurate and available.
6. Data, Application & Platform Governance
- Oversee application architecture, integrations, and data flows.
- Ensure data handling and platform operations align with contractual, regulatory, and security requirements.
- Maintain observability, performance monitoring, and reliability engineering practices.
- Oversee architecture for AI, data, and analytics platforms to support scalable model development, deployment, and observability.
7. Vendor & Third-Party Technology Management
- Select, evaluate, and manage technology vendors and platforms.
- Ensure third-party tools and services meet architectural, security, and compliance requirements.
- Maintain visibility into vendor dependencies and integrations.
8. Program Execution & Delivery
- Lead execution of major technical initiatives, platform deployments, and releases.
- Translate business and product requirements into governed technical delivery plans.
- Track delivery risks, dependencies, and milestones.
9. Team Leadership & Technical Oversight
- Build, lead, and mentor engineering and platform teams.
- Define roles, responsibilities, and accountability within technology functions.
- Ensure appropriate segregation of duties across engineering, operations, and security.
10. Authority & Decision Rights
- Authority to define and enforce technology standards and architectural patterns.
- Authority to approve system designs, tooling selections, and platform implementations.
- Authority to halt deployments that violate architectural, reliability, or compliance requirements.
- Escalation authority to executive leadership for material technology risks.
11. Explicit Role Boundaries
- The CTO does not own cybersecurity policy, risk acceptance, or security governance authority.
- Formal security policy, risk decisions, and control ownership reside with the CISO or designated security leadership.
- The CTO does not replace formally assigned SOC 2 or CMMC control owners.
12. Qualifications
- 10+ years of progressive technology leadership experience.
- Strong background in cloud platforms, modern application architectures, and DevSecOps.
- Demonstrated experience operating in regulated or compliance-driven environments.
13. Success Measures
- Stable, scalable, and auditable technology platforms.
- Successful SOC 2 and CMMC Level 2 audit outcomes with minimal findings.
- Predictable delivery of technical initiatives.
- Clear documentation and architectural visibility.

descriptions.text:
Cybersecurity Analyst
Position Description - Cloud Security, IAM, Incident Response, and Governance
Position Summary
The Cybersecurity Analyst will help design, implement, monitor, and improve DriverAI’s cybersecurity program across cloud, endpoint, identity, collaboration, and business technology environments. This role manages security applications, supports security response processes, administers identity and access management for Microsoft 365, SharePoint, and related cloud services, and helps ensure security controls align with business, compliance, and operational requirements.
The ideal candidate is a hands-on cybersecurity professional who can identify security events, assess risk, mitigate threats, coordinate incident resolution, evaluate commercial security tools, implement best-practice controls, draft and validate policies, and contribute to SOC 2 and CMMC Level 2 readiness. This position requires strong technical judgment, attention to detail, clear documentation, and the ability to balance security, usability, mission alignment, and business value.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
Cloud Security and Security Application Management
Manage, configure, monitor, and maintain cybersecurity platforms and tools supporting cloud, endpoint, network, identity, and collaboration environments.
Support security operations for cloud network environments, including alert review, investigation, response coordination, remediation tracking, and closure validation.
Implement and maintain security controls for cloud services, including logging, access control, encryption, monitoring, endpoint protection, vulnerability management, and secure configuration baselines.
Assist with security architecture reviews for new cloud services, applications, integrations, and infrastructure changes.
Support security applications throughout the product lifecycle, including evaluation, deployment, configuration, tuning, maintenance, upgrades, and retirement.
Review security alerts, triage potential threats, document findings, and coordinate corrective actions with technical teams and service providers.
Incident Response Identification, Mitigation, and Resolution
Identify potential cybersecurity incidents across endpoints, cloud services, Microsoft 365, SharePoint, identity systems, email, collaboration platforms, and network resources.
Analyze alerts, logs, endpoint telemetry, user reports, identity activity, and cloud security events to determine incident scope, severity, impact, and priority.
Perform or coordinate initial containment and mitigation actions, including account lockout, credential reset, access revocation, device isolation, quarantine, blocking indicators of compromise, policy adjustment, and escalation to MDR, SOC, IT, cloud, or engineering teams.
Support root-cause analysis and determine whether incidents involve misconfiguration, credential compromise, malware, phishing, unauthorized access, policy violations, or control gaps.
Track incidents from identification through mitigation, remediation, validation, and final resolution.
Document incident timelines, affected systems, evidence reviewed, actions taken, business impact, lessons learned, and preventive recommendations.
Support post-incident reviews and help convert lessons learned into updated controls, playbooks, policies, procedures, and user guidance.
Develop and refine incident response playbooks, escalation paths, response checklists, automated response workflows, and resolution criteria.
Identity and Access Management
Administer IAM for Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Entra ID/Azure AD, and related cloud services.
Manage user access, roles, permissions, groups, conditional access policies, MFA settings, and privileged access controls.
Support onboarding, offboarding, access reviews, and least-privilege enforcement.
Monitor and review identity-related risks, including suspicious sign-ins, excessive permissions, dormant accounts, privilege escalation, and unusual access patterns.
Assist in developing and enforcing role-based access control policies and procedures.
Security Governance, Policies, and Procedures
Validate, draft, update, and maintain cybersecurity, network, cloud, IAM, acceptable use, data protection, incident response, access control, and security operations policies and procedures.
Ensure security policies are practical, enforceable, and aligned with business operations, customer requirements, and compliance obligations.
Support governance activities related to SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST SP 800-171, and other applicable cybersecurity frameworks.
Assist with control implementation, evidence collection, gap assessments, remediation tracking, audit readiness, and corrective action closure.
Maintain documentation for security configurations, procedures, tool usage, incident response actions, incident resolution evidence, and compliance records.
Security Tool Assessment and Mission Alignment
Research, evaluate, and compare commercial cybersecurity platforms and tools based on cost, value, capability, integration, security impact, automation potential, and mission alignment.
Assess whether tools support organizational security goals, compliance needs, scalability, automation, and operational efficiency.
Recommend improvements to existing security tools, workflows, response processes, and control implementations.
Work with leadership and technical teams to prioritize security investments based on risk, business value, mission impact, and operational requirements.
Required Qualifications
Minimum of one year supporting cybersecurity operations, cloud security, IAM, endpoint security, incident response, or security tool administration.
Practical experience with Microsoft 365 administration and SharePoint user/access management. Familiarity with Entra ID/Azure AD, cloud collaboration tools, and core identity management concepts.
Demonstrated understanding of least privilege, multi-factor authentication, conditional access, encryption, secure logging, vulnerability management, endpoint protection, and baseline configuration enforcement.
Ability to identify and investigate security alerts, assess incident severity, document findings, coordinate mitigation, and support incident resolution.
Experience drafting or maintaining security documentation, policies, procedures, playbooks, or technical guidance.
Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently while coordinating across technical, business, vendor, and leadership teams.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST SP 800-171, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 27001, or similar security frameworks.
Experience with commercial cybersecurity platforms such as SentinelOne, Microsoft Defender, CrowdStrike, Check Point, Palo Alto, Okta, Duo, Splunk, Wiz, Vanta, Drata, or similar tools.
Experience supporting cloud environments such as AWS, Azure, Microsoft 365, or hybrid cloud architectures.
Familiarity with security tool selection, vendor evaluation, cost-benefit analysis, automation, and mission alignment assessments.
Experience supporting MDR, SIEM, EDR, vulnerability scanning, cloud security posture management, incident response automation, or compliance automation tools.
Certifications such as Security+, CySA+, SSCP, CISSP Associate, Microsoft Security, AWS Security Specialty, CISM, or equivalent experience.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Strong understanding of cloud security, IAM, endpoint protection, network security, and incident response fundamentals.
Ability to translate cybersecurity requirements into practical operational procedures and response playbooks.
Ability to evaluate risk, prioritize mitigation, coordinate remediation, validate resolution, and communicate security issues clearly.
Strong documentation skills for policies, procedures, evidence collection, incident records, technical guidance, and compliance support.
Ability to manage security services throughout the product lifecycle.
Working knowledge of governance, risk, compliance, incident management, and security operations concepts.
Ability to support both tactical security operations and strategic cybersecurity program improvement.
Position Details
Company: DriverAI
Position Type: Full-time or part-time options may be considered based on candidate qualifications and company needs.
Work Location: Remote, hybrid, or company-designated location based on operational requirements.
Application: Send Resume to Apply @DriverAI.io

Cybersecurity & IT Administrator Manager Position Description

Role Summary
The Cybersecurity & IT Administrator Manager is responsible for the day-to-day execution and operational management of the organization’s information security program and IT administration activities. Reporting to the CISO, this role ensures that security policies, procedures, controls, and monitoring activities are implemented effectively and operate as designed. The role supports audit readiness, incident response, and continuous risk reduction while coordinating IT administration activities with the CTO and engineering leadership.

Primary cybersecurity and IT administration responsibilities remain the core focus of this role. Property management oversight and support of intern-led asset management activities are secondary responsibilities performed to maintain operational accountability and chain-of-custody integrity.
The role also uses approved AI tools and analytical methods to support security analysis, operational reporting, ticket triage, documentation, control review, trend identification, and continuous improvement, while protecting sensitive company, customer, and security information.

Core Responsibilities

1. Security Operations Management
- Manage daily security operations across cloud, endpoint, network, and application environments.
- Oversee EDR, SIEM, vulnerability scanning, monitoring, and alert management platforms.
- Ensure security incidents and operational events are triaged, documented, escalated, and resolved appropriately.

2. AI Tools, Analysis & Operational Decision Support
- Use approved AI-enabled tools to assist with cybersecurity analysis, IT operations review, alert triage, documentation, reporting, and workflow improvement.
- Analyze security, IT, endpoint, identity, vulnerability, asset, and compliance data to identify trends, risks, recurring issues, and improvement opportunities.
- Support development of AI-assisted summaries, dashboards, evidence packages, response notes, knowledge articles, and operational recommendations when authorized.
- Validate AI-assisted outputs for accuracy, relevance, confidentiality, and alignment with company policy before use or distribution.
- Ensure AI tool usage follows approved data protection, privacy, access control, and confidentiality requirements.

3. Governance, Risk & Compliance Execution
- Implement security policies, standards, and procedures defined by the CISO.
- Support SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST, and related compliance activities.
- Maintain audit artifacts, evidence, logs, and supporting documentation.

4. Vulnerability, Patch & Endpoint Management
- Coordinate vulnerability scanning and remediation activities.
- Ensure timely operating system, application, and infrastructure patching.
- Manage endpoint security controls including encryption, MDM, endpoint protection, and configuration baselines.

5. Identity & Access Management
- Administer provisioning, deprovisioning, and access lifecycle management.
- Support MFA, SSO, RBAC, and periodic access recertification processes.
- Enforce least-privilege principles and privileged access monitoring.

6. Incident Response & Operational Support
- Execute incident response procedures including containment, recovery, and evidence preservation.
- Support root cause analysis and corrective action implementation.
- Coordinate operational support activities with engineering and cloud teams.

7. IT Administration & Systems Support
- Oversee day-to-day IT administration activities including workstations, SaaS platforms, servers, and collaboration tools.
- Manage onboarding/offboarding activities, account provisioning, and endpoint readiness.
- Maintain backup, restore, and recovery validation activities.

8. Property Management & Asset Oversight (Secondary Responsibility)
- Oversee intern-supported IT asset management and chain-of-custody activities.
- Validate inventory accuracy, asset tagging, custody tracking, and deployment documentation.
- Ensure device staging, deployment preparation, and equipment disposition activities follow approved procedures.
- Review and approve intern-submitted asset records, checklists, and operational documentation.
- Support periodic physical and logical inventory audits.

9. Intern Supervision & Operational Development
- Provide operational guidance and supervision to Cybersecurity & IT Intern personnel.
- Ensure interns follow approved security, confidentiality, and asset handling procedures.
- Support intern development through exposure to SOC 2, CMMC, and operational security practices.

10. Change, Configuration & Service Management
- Enforce change management and configuration control processes.
- Participate in Change Advisory Board (CAB) activities as assigned.
- Ensure operational changes are documented, reviewed, tested, and approved.

11. Reporting & Continuous Improvement
- Track operational KPIs, control effectiveness, and remediation activities.
- Escalate unresolved operational risks and control gaps to the CISO and CTO.
- Recommend process improvements to strengthen operational efficiency and security posture.

12. Other Duties as Assigned
- Perform other cybersecurity, IT administration, compliance, asset management, AI-assisted analysis, documentation, operational support, and related duties as assigned based on business, security, customer, or organizational needs.

Authority & Decision Rights
- Authority to execute approved security and IT operational procedures.
- Authority to escalate operational risks, incidents, and control failures.
- Accountability for operational effectiveness of assigned security and IT controls.
- Does not own cybersecurity policy, risk acceptance, or technology architecture authority.

Qualifications
- 5–8 years of experience in cybersecurity, IT administration, or related operational roles.
- Experience supporting cloud, endpoint, and operational security environments.
- Familiarity with SOC 2, CMMC, NIST 800-171, or related frameworks.
- Strong documentation, operational discipline, and organizational skills.
- Ability to use approved AI tools responsibly to support analysis, documentation, reporting, workflow improvement, and decision support while validating outputs and protecting sensitive information.

descriptions.text:
DRIVERAI
IT & Cybersecurity Administrator
Job Announcement
Position Overview
DriverAI is seeking an IT & Cybersecurity Administrator to support secure daily operations across commercial and government-focused environments. This role combines hands-on IT administration, cybersecurity support, endpoint and identity management, cloud and collaboration platform support, documentation control, and compliance readiness activities that help keep systems secure, users supported, and records audit-ready.
This position is well suited for a disciplined, detail-oriented professional who can execute approved operational controls, manage user and endpoint support tasks, document work accurately, coordinate across technical teams, and contribute to a mature, scalable security and technology environment.
Role Summary
• Supports cybersecurity monitoring, IT administration, endpoint readiness, and user support operations.
• Administers accounts, permissions, MFA, provisioning, and related identity lifecycle tasks.
• Maintains documentation, inventories, evidence files, and procedural records supporting operational discipline and compliance.
• Assists with incident response support, vulnerability follow-up, secure configuration tasks, and change control activities.
• Provides secondary support for property accountability, asset custody tracking, and device lifecycle processes.
Primary Duties and Responsibilities
1. Security Operations and Monitoring – Supports daily operational security activities that help identify, contain, escalate, and document cybersecurity issues.
• Monitor alerts, logs, endpoint telemetry, identity events, email security signals, and related operational indicators.
• Review potential threats and suspicious activity, document findings, and coordinate escalation or corrective actions with the CISO, CTO, MDR, MSP, or other designated providers.
• Support endpoint, identity, cloud, email, and collaboration security operations across Microsoft 365, Entra ID, cloud-hosted services, and related environments.
• Assist with vulnerability review, remediation coordination, and validation of closure for operationally assigned items.
2. IT Administration and Endpoint Management – Maintains operational technology services and endpoint readiness to support a secure, stable, and productive environment.
• Administer user workstations, laptops, approved mobile-supporting systems, SaaS platforms, collaboration tools, printers, and related IT resources as assigned.
• Support user onboarding, offboarding, account provisioning, system setup, device deployment, software installation, patching, and secure baseline configuration.
• Maintain endpoint encryption, endpoint protection, patch compliance, backup coordination, and general operational readiness.
• Support troubleshooting, issue tracking, ticket coordination, and timely follow-through on user and operational support needs.
3. Identity and Access Management – Supports secure access administration to reduce risk and maintain accountability for users, systems, and privileged actions.
• Administer user accounts, groups, roles, shared resources, multi-factor authentication, conditional access settings, and permissions within approved systems.
• Support least-privilege enforcement, role-based access administration, and periodic account and access reviews.
• Assist with account lockout, credential reset, access revocation, privileged account tracking, and user lifecycle actions.
• Help verify that terminated, transferred, inactive, or unnecessary access is removed in a timely manner.
4. Governance, Compliance, and Documentation – Maintains records and operational evidence that support governance, audit readiness, and repeatable execution.
• Maintain procedures, system records, inventories, evidence files, control artifacts, remediation trackers, and other documentation supporting operational and compliance requirements.
• Support readiness activities for SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST SP 800-171, and other applicable customer or regulatory requirements.
• Assist in validating that operational practices align with approved policies, standards, procedures, and configuration requirements.
• Track corrective actions, open items, and operational follow-up tasks through closure or escalation.
5. Incident Response and Operational Security Support – Supports timely, organized response to security incidents and operational control failures.
• Assist with identification, triage, containment, escalation, remediation support, and documentation of cybersecurity incidents or suspected incidents.
• Preserve and organize relevant logs, records, screenshots, timeline notes, and other evidence required for internal review or external support.
• Support root-cause analysis, lessons learned, and follow-up actions designed to reduce recurrence and improve control effectiveness.
• Coordinate with leadership and service providers regarding incident notifications, tasking, and status updates.
6. Change, Configuration, and Operational Control – Supports disciplined technology changes and configuration management to reduce avoidable risk.
• Follow approved change management, configuration control, and deployment procedures for assigned systems and services.
• Document significant system, account, endpoint, or operational changes and maintain records needed for traceability and review.
• Help validate secure configuration baselines, version control practices, and deployment readiness for operational changes.
• Coordinate with technical leads when planned changes may affect security posture, access, availability, or compliance obligations.
7. Asset Oversight, Property Accountability, and Lifecycle Support – Provides secondary support to preserve accountability and control across device inventory and custody activities.
• Support oversight of asset inventory, equipment assignment, custody tracking, device staging, deployment, return, storage, and disposition records.
• Help maintain chain-of-custody documentation for assigned IT assets and sensitive devices, especially where commercial and government requirements differ.
• Assist with inventory reconciliation, audit support, and lifecycle status verification for laptops, accessories, and related equipment.
• Validate intern-supported asset management activities for accuracy, completeness, and procedural compliance.
8. Intern Coordination and Operational Guidance – Provides structured operational direction for intern-supported work as assigned.
• Provide day-to-day task guidance, procedural clarification, and quality review for Cybersecurity and IT Intern personnel when delegated.
• Ensure interns follow approved instructions for confidentiality, device handling, recordkeeping, and chain-of-custody accountability.
• Escalate performance, process, or security concerns involving intern-supported work when necessary.
What Success Looks Like
• Secure and dependable operational support across endpoints, accounts, and technology platforms.
• Accurate and timely completion of documentation, tickets, evidence, and assigned action items.
• Strong support for audit readiness, compliance objectives, and operational accountability.
• Professional communication, reliable follow-through, and effective cross-team coordination.
• Timely escalation of issues, incidents, risks, and unresolved control concerns.
Required Qualifications
• Experience in IT administration, cybersecurity operations, endpoint management, cloud-connected support, or a related operational role.
• Familiarity with Microsoft 365, account administration, identity and access management concepts, MFA, and operational security controls.
• Working knowledge of patching, endpoint readiness, secure configurations, documentation control, and issue follow-through.
• Strong communication, organization, and documentation skills.
• Ability to manage operational priorities while coordinating with leadership, users, vendors, and technical teams.
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience with AWS, Azure, Microsoft 365, SIEM, EDR, MDM, IAM, vulnerability management, or ticketing platforms.
• Familiarity with SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST SP 800-171, or other regulated environment requirements.
• Experience supporting government-related, compliance-driven, or audit-sensitive operating environments.
• Security+, CySA+, SSCP, Microsoft Security, AWS, or equivalent certifications preferred.
Why Join DriverAI
• Work directly with cybersecurity, cloud, engineering, and executive leadership in a growing technology environment.
• Contribute to both commercial and government-focused operational initiatives.
• Gain hands-on experience supporting modern security, compliance, cloud, and endpoint management practices.
• Join a team building structured, scalable, and mission-aligned technology operations.
Position Details
• Company: DriverAI
• Position Type: Full-time; part-time options may be considered based on company needs.
• Work Location: Remote, hybrid, or company-designated location based on operational requirements.
• Application: Submit resume and relevant qualifications for consideration.

descriptions.title: Cybersecurity IT Administrator Position
descriptions.text:
Role Summary
The Cybersecurity and IT Administrator is responsible for the day-to-day execution and operational management of the organization’s information security program. Reporting to the CISO, this role ensures that security policies, procedures, controls, and monitoring activities are implemented effectively and operate as designed. The Cybersecurity and IT Administrator translates security strategy into operational reality and supports audit readiness, incident response, and continuous risk reduction. This role does not own security policy, risk acceptance, or technology architecture decisions; those responsibilities remain with the CISO and CTO respectively.

While the cybersecurity role reports to the CISO, responsibility for technology architecture and system ownership remains with the CTO; IT administration activities are performed in coordination with the CTO and engineering leadership.

Core Responsibilities
1. Security Operations Management
- Manage daily security operations across cloud, endpoint, network, and application environments.
- Oversee security tooling including EDR, SIEM, vulnerability scanners, and monitoring platforms.
- Ensure alerts, incidents, and events are triaged, investigated, and resolved in accordance with procedures.

2. Governance, Risk & Compliance Execution
- Implement and maintain security policies, standards, and procedures defined by the CISO.
- Support SOC 2, CMMC, NIST, and other compliance activities through evidence collection and control operation.
- Maintain security documentation, logs, and audit artifacts.

3. Vulnerability & Patch Management
- Coordinate vulnerability scanning, risk prioritization, and remediation tracking.
- Ensure timely patching of operating systems, applications, and infrastructure.
- Validate remediation effectiveness and report risk metrics.

4. Incident Response Support
- Execute incident response procedures, including detection, containment, eradication, and recovery.
- Maintain incident tickets, timelines, and evidence.
- Support tabletop exercises and post-incident reviews.

5. Identity & Access Management Operations
- Administer user access provisioning, deprovisioning, and role changes.
- Monitor privileged access and enforce least-privilege principles.
- Support and execute MFA, SSO, and periodic access review/recertification processes, documenting results and remediation.

6. Endpoint & Asset Security
- Manage device security controls including encryption, MDM, and endpoint protection.
- Track asset inventory and ensure secure configuration baselines.
- Support secure asset disposal and data destruction processes.

7. Vendor & Third-Party Security Support
- Assist with vendor security assessments and ongoing monitoring.
- Track remediation of third-party security findings.
- Maintain vendor security records.

8. Security Awareness & Training
- Coordinate security awareness training and phishing simulations.
- Track training completion and compliance.
- Reinforce security best practices with staff.

9. Metrics, Reporting & Continuous Improvement
- Track operational security KPIs and metrics.
- Identify control gaps and improvement opportunities.
- Report operational security status to the CISO.

Qualifications
- 5–8 years of experience in information security or IT operations.
- Hands-on experience with security tools, monitoring, and incident response.
- Familiarity with SOC 2, NIST 800-171, CMMC, or similar frameworks.
- Strong documentation and operational discipline.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience in cloud security environments (AWS preferred).
- Exposure to audits, assessments, or regulated industries.
- Relevant certifications (e.g., Security+, SSCP, CISSP Associate).

Key Competencies
- Operational execution and attention to detail
- Incident handling and troubleshooting
- Risk awareness and prioritization
- Clear communication and documentation
- Collaboration across IT and engineering teams

Authority & Decision Rights
- Authority to execute approved security procedures and controls.
- Escalation authority for security incidents and control failures.
- Accountability for operational effectiveness of security controls.

Additional IT Administration & Team Management Responsibilities
10. IT Systems & Administration
-  Oversee day-to-day IT administration including user workstations, servers, SaaS platforms, and collaboration tools.
- Manage MDM/RMM platforms, endpoint configuration baselines, backups, and system availability.
- Coordinate onboarding and offboarding activities, including account provisioning, asset assignment, and access revocation.
- Ensure system documentation, inventories, and configuration records remain accurate and audit-ready.
- Support business continuity and disaster recovery procedures from an IT operations perspective.
- Execute and document regular backup and restore tests, and report any failures or gaps to the CISO and CTO.

11. IT & Security Team Management
- Supervise and mentor staff across security and IT operations functions.
- Assign tasks, manage workloads, and ensure proper separation of duties across teams.
- Support hiring, training, and performance management for IT and security personnel.
- Act as escalation point for technical and operational issues within IT and security teams.
- Foster collaboration between IT, engineering, security, and business stakeholders.

12. Change, Configuration & Service Management
- Enforce change management and configuration control processes for IT and security systems.
- Participate in or lead Change Advisory Board (CAB) activities as assigned.
- Track IT service issues, requests, and remediation efforts.
- Ensure operational changes are documented, tested, and approved prior to implementation.

descriptions.title: Data Analyst Position Description
descriptions.text:
Position Title: Data Analyst
Department: Engineering
Reports To: Chief Technology Officer, Data Science Lead
Position Type: Full-time, part-time, or internship
Work Environment: Remote
Position Summary
The Data Analyst collects, organizes, analyzes, and translates data into useful business insights that support company goals, such as making informed decisions, improving operations, developing products, understanding customers, and measuring performance. Strong analytical judgment, coding skills, dashboard development, and the ability to assess complex data are essential. Data sources include structured databases, unstructured text, logs, websites, cloud services, and real-time user feedback.
The Data Analyst develops KPIs, dashboards, analytical models, reports, and repeatable processes to help teams and stakeholders understand trends, assess risks, measure results, and improve outcomes.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Data Collection, Scraping, and Preparation
Collect, clean, validate, normalize, and transform data from databases, spreadsheets, cloud platforms, APIs, websites, application logs, third-party tools, and business systems.
Develop and maintain automated processes for getting, changing, loading, and extracting data, including scraping data from websites or other digital sources, where it is legal and fits business needs.
Use approved data scraping and automation tools to gather authorized or publicly available data for market research, customer insights, competitive intelligence, pricing analysis, operational monitoring, and business reporting.
Identify data quality issues, missing data, duplicate records, inconsistent formatting, unreliable sources, and data integrity concerns, and recommend corrective actions.
Ensure collected data is accurate, complete, secure, and documented. Align all data with company policies, privacy rules, and compliance obligations.
Data Analysis and Critical Evaluation
Perform detailed analysis to find trends (patterns over time), patterns (repeating data), and connections between data. Identify unusual results (anomalies), root causes of problems, risks, and new business opportunities.
Analyze customer behavior, operational performance, and system usage. Assess product adoption, process efficiency, revenue drivers, marketing impact, and service results.
Use statistical methods, data exploration, grouping, forecasting, and comparison. Use these to help business and technical decisions.
Translate raw data into clear findings and business implications. Provide executive summaries and recommend actions for leadership and technical teams.
Conduct ad hoc analysis in response to urgent business questions, operational issues, product concerns, or emerging opportunities.
Real-Time Data Feedback Loops
Support the design and implementation of real-time or near-real-time data feedback loops to improve product performance, operational visibility, and decision-making.
Monitor incoming data streams from applications, user interactions, system events, cloud platforms, customer touchpoints, sensors, and other business systems.
Develop analytical processes to help teams quickly detect changes in performance, user behavior, reliability, engagement, and risk.
Work with engineering and product teams to decide which events to track. Determine how to collect usage data (telemetry), label data (tagging), move data between systems (data pipelines), and set up feedback mechanisms.
Recommend process, product, or system improvements based on continuous data feedback.
KPI, Metrics, and Dashboard Development
Define, develop, and maintain KPIs, metrics, scorecards, and dashboards that match business goals.
Build dashboards and reports that give leaders and teams timely views of performance.
Create dashboards for executive reporting, product analytics, operations, customer insights, marketing, finance trends, compliance, and project tracking.
Create drill-down reports, automated alerts, trend views, exception reports, and summaries of performance.
Ensure dashboards are accurate, visually effective, easy to interpret, and designed to support decision-making.
Coding, Automation, and Technical Development
Write scripts and queries to extract, transform, analyze, visualize, and check data. Build automation workflows for these tasks.
Use languages such as Python, SQL, R, JavaScript, or similar tools to analyze data and automate tasks.
Develop reusable scripts, notebooks, workflows, templates, and documentation to support recurring analysis.
Work with APIs, cloud platforms, databases, and analytics tools. Combine data from various systems.
Support data pipeline building, workflow automation, and report automation with engineering or IT teams.
Tools and Technology
Data Analysis: Python and R for programming, SQL for database queries, Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets for spreadsheets, and Jupyter Notebook for coding and sharing analysis.
Visualization and Dashboards: Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Google Looker Studio, Grafana, Metabase, or similar business intelligence tools (platforms for creating visual reports from data).
Databases and Warehouses: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, or similar platforms.
Data Scraping and Automation: BeautifulSoup, Selenium, Scrapy, Requests, APIs, browser automation tools, or approved commercial scraping tools (programs used to gather data from the web).
Cloud and Data Platforms: Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, cloud storage, cloud databases, and analytics services.
Collaboration and Documentation: Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, Confluence, Jira, GitHub, GitLab, or similar tools.
Governance and Security: Access controls, data classification, privacy protection, data retention, and secure handling of sensitive information.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Business Analytics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Economics, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.
Experience collecting, cleaning, analyzing, and visualizing business or technical data.
Proficiency with SQL and at least one coding or scripting language such as Python, R, or JavaScript.
Experience developing dashboards, reports, KPIs, and business performance metrics.
Ability to conduct complex analysis and explain findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience working with structured and unstructured data from multiple sources.
Strong attention to detail, analytical thinking, problem-solving ability, and documentation skills.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively across technical, business, and leadership teams.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with web scraping, API-based data collection, and automated data pipelines.
Experience supporting real-time or near-real-time analytics, telemetry, application usage data, or operational monitoring.
Experience with cloud-based analytics platforms such as AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Snowflake, Redshift, or BigQuery.
Familiarity with artificial intelligence, machine learning, predictive analytics, customer analytics, or product analytics.
Experience developing dashboards for executive leadership, product teams, operations, marketing, or compliance reporting.
Experience with data governance, privacy, cybersecurity, or compliance-focused reporting.
Familiarity with version control tools such as GitHub or GitLab.
Core Competencies
Critical thinking and complex problem solving; data-driven decision support; technical coding and automation.
Dashboard and KPI development; data visualization and storytelling; business process analysis.
Data quality and validation; cross-functional communication; secure and ethical data handling; continuous improvement mindset.
Performance Expectations
Accuracy, completeness, and usefulness of analytical outputs.
Quality and reliability of dashboards, KPIs, reports, and automated workflows.
Ability to identify trends, risks, opportunities, root causes, and measurable business impacts.
Support for real-time data feedback loops and operational decision-making.
Timely, clear communication with stakeholders and strong documentation of methods, assumptions, and sources.

You will support leadership, product, engineering, operations, and business teams by collecting, analyzing, visualizing, and assessing data from multiple sources.

Strong analytical (critical thinking), quantitative, and problem-solving skills.
Proficiency in SQL and advanced data analysis tools is required.

Collect and analyze data from multiple sources. Use APIs, spreadsheets, databases, cloud systems, and web-based sources.

Clearly communicate findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Demonstrate attention to detail and proven ability to validate data accuracy is critical.
Demonstrated ability to work independently, prioritize multiple tasks, and manage dynamic business requirements.

Experience with data scraping tools such as BeautifulSoup, Selenium, Scrapy, Requests, or similar technologies.
Experience with cloud data platforms such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery, or similar systems.
Support real-time analytics, telemetry, and application monitoring. Contribute to product analytics or operational feedback loops.
Familiarity with artificial intelligence, machine learning, predictive analytics, or advanced analytics techniques.
Experience with GitHub, GitLab, Jira, SharePoint, Microsoft 365, or similar collaboration tools.
Experience with data governance, cybersecurity reporting, privacy requirements, or compliance-driven analytics.
Develop executive dashboards. Contribute to creating performance measurement frameworks.
Tools and Technologies
SQL; Python, R, or JavaScript; Microsoft Excel and advanced spreadsheet modeling.
Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Grafana, Metabase, or similar dashboard tools.
APIs, data scraping tools, cloud data platforms, databases, and data visualization tools.
GitHub or similar version control tools; Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, and related collaboration platforms.
Ideal Candidate
The ideal candidate is curious and a technically capable analyst with business insight, providing deeper assessments beyond surface-level deductions. Candidates ask the right questions, evaluate data critically, and automate recurring analysis. Develop meaningful KPIs and build dashboards. Helps by creating real-time feedback loops that improve performance and data-driven decision-making.
This role fits someone who is analytical, detail-oriented, and proactive in learning new tools. If you excel at working with data and solving complex problems and enjoy guiding teams using evidence-based analysis, you will thrive in this position.
Education and Experience
·         Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Business Analytics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Economics, or a related field preferred.
Equivalent technical experience, portfolio projects, certifications, internships, or other analytical work may be considered.
·         Experience in a startup, technology company, product environment, operations team, or business intelligence role is highly desirable.
Position Type
Full-time, part-time, or internship options may be considered. Choices will depend on the candidate’s qualifications and business needs.
Summary Statement for Posting
We are looking for a Data Analyst who can turn complex data into clear business intelligence visualizations. The successful candidate will support data scraping, coding, dashboard development, KPI tracking, and the development of real-time feedback assessments. Use critical analysis to help the company improve products, operations, customer insights, and strategic decision-making.

descriptions.text:
Job Announcement: Data Engineer
Data Analytics Support, AWS-Integrated Data Workflows, and Business Intelligence Enablement
DriverAI | Internal / Recruiting Use

About DriverAI
DriverAI is a technology startup developing intelligent indoor location, navigation, analytics, artificial intelligence, computer vision, and data-driven solutions for complex physical environments. Our work supports smarter indoor navigation, product discovery, operational insight, real-time feedback, and better decision-making for commercial, retail, and technology-driven environments.
About the Role
We are seeking a technically capable and detail-oriented Data Engineer to help build and maintain the data foundation that supports our analytics, dashboards, product intelligence, cloud infrastructure, artificial intelligence workflows, and business operations.
The Data Engineer will support the Data Analytics team by building reliable data pipelines, organizing data sources, automating data workflows, improving data quality, and enabling dashboards, reporting, key performance indicators, and business intelligence functions.
This role will also interface with AWS infrastructure to support cloud-based data storage, processing, integration, monitoring, and analytics workflows. The successful candidate will work across data analytics, software development, cloud infrastructure, AI/ML, computer vision, cybersecurity, product, and leadership teams.
Key Responsibilities
Build, maintain, and improve data pipelines for analytics, reporting, dashboards, machine learning, and product intelligence.
Collect, ingest, clean, transform, validate, and organize data from applications, databases, APIs, cloud services, logs, telemetry, business systems, and approved external sources.
Support AWS-based data workflows using services such as S3, RDS, Redshift, Glue, Athena, Lambda, CloudWatch, DynamoDB, QuickSight, EC2, ECS, EKS, and API Gateway as applicable.
Develop SQL queries, database views, schemas, data models, and analytics-ready datasets.
Automate recurring data processing, validation, reporting, and monitoring tasks using Python, SQL, scripts, and cloud-native services.
Work with Data Analysts to support dashboards, KPIs, business intelligence, product analytics, and real-time or near-real-time feedback loops.
Support data quality through validation checks, anomaly detection, reconciliation, monitoring, and troubleshooting.
Integrate data from internal applications, third-party systems, APIs, mobile and web applications, logs, and product telemetry.
Support event tracking, application analytics, product usage data, indoor mapping data, computer vision outputs, and AI/ML-related data workflows.
Document data sources, pipeline logic, transformation rules, data assumptions, schemas, dependencies, and troubleshooting procedures.
Collaborate with AWS infrastructure, software development, cybersecurity, AI/ML, computer vision, product, and leadership teams.
Follow secure data handling practices, including least-privilege access, encryption awareness, data minimization, controlled access, and appropriate documentation.
Support governance, audit readiness, SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST-aligned control evidence, or other compliance-related documentation when applicable.
Required Skills and Experience
Strong SQL skills and experience working with databases or analytics systems.
Experience using Python or another scripting language for data processing, automation, or integration.
Understanding of data pipelines, ETL/ELT workflows, data modeling, data quality, and analytics enablement.
Experience working with cloud-based data platforms or cloud infrastructure; AWS experience is preferred.
Familiarity with relational databases, cloud databases, object storage, data warehouses, data lakes, or NoSQL databases.
Ability to troubleshoot data issues, broken pipelines, query problems, integration errors, and inconsistent analytics outputs.
Ability to document technical workflows clearly and maintain organized data engineering artifacts.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills.
Ability to work independently while coordinating with team leads and cross-functional contributors.
Preferred Skills
Experience with AWS data services such as S3, Glue, Athena, Redshift, RDS, DynamoDB, Lambda, CloudWatch, EC2, ECS, EKS, API Gateway, or QuickSight.
Experience with Airflow, Prefect, Dagster, AWS Step Functions, dbt, Spark, PySpark, Pandas, or similar tools.
Experience supporting dashboards or business intelligence tools such as Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Grafana, Amazon QuickSight, Metabase, or similar platforms.
Experience with APIs, JSON, application logs, web scraping, telemetry, event tracking, product analytics, or real-time data processing.
Familiarity with Git, GitHub, GitLab, Jira, SharePoint, Microsoft 365, Docker, CI/CD, Terraform, CloudFormation, or other collaborative development and deployment tools.
Experience supporting AI, machine learning, computer vision, retail analytics, indoor mapping, product recognition, or other data-intensive technology environments.
Knowledge of data governance, data lineage, metadata management, privacy-aware data handling, access controls, and secure cloud practices.
Familiarity with SOC 2, CMMC Level 2, NIST SP 800-171, ISO 27001, or similar governance and cybersecurity frameworks is a plus.
Ideal Candidate
The ideal candidate is a practical data builder who enjoys turning raw, fragmented, or unreliable data into structured, trusted, and usable information. This person understands that effective analytics depends on strong pipelines, clean data, clear definitions, and reliable cloud infrastructure.
The right candidate is detail-oriented, technically curious, comfortable working with AWS and databases, and able to support both technical teams and business users. They can troubleshoot data problems, automate repetitive work, document clearly, and help the company make better decisions through stronger data systems.

Bachelor's degree in Data Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Science, Software Engineering, Cloud Computing, Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Analytics, or a related field is preferred.
